Year:1894       ACT NO.:637
AN ACT TO AMEND THE " ACT TO INCORPORATE THE BOARD OF VISITORS OF THE THORNWELL ORPHANAGE , AND TO AUTHORIZE THE CLINTON PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH TO TRANSFER CERTAIN PROPERTY TO THE SAME , " APPROVED 24TH DECEMBER , 1888 .

Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the State of South Carolina , now met and sitting in Gen- eral Assembly , and by the authority of the same , That an A. A. 1888 Act to incorporate the Board of Visitors of the Thornwell Orphanage and to authorize the Clinton Presbyterian Church to transfer certain property to the same , ratified 24th December , 1888 , be amended so that the same shall read as follows :

Section 1. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Rep- resentatives of the State of South Carolina , now met and sit- ting in General Assembly , and by the authority of the same , That William P. Jacobs , Pastor , M. S. Bailey , R. S. Phinny , and other Elders , and A. M. Copeland , G. C. Young and others , Deacons of the Clinton Presbyterian Church , and their successors in office duly appointed , together with any seven persons appointed by the Synod of South Carolina , five persons by the Synod of Georgia , three persons by the Synod of South Georgia and Florida , and two persons by any one of the other Synods connected with the Presbyterian Church in the United States , be , and they are hereby , created a body corporate and politic , to be known under the name and style of the " Board of Visitors of the Thorn- well Orphanage , " for the purpose of supporting , maintain-
ing and educating white orphans or children of reputable parentage , one of whom is dead . The Board of Visitors by said name shall have perpetual succession of officers and members , and a common seal , with power to change , alter , and make anew the same , as often as the said Board may deem expedient . The said Board in case any Synod shall fail to appoint representatives as hereinbefore specified may appoint to said office such person or persons as it may select , resident within the bounds of the said Synod , under such provision as it may adopt .

Sec . 2. That the said Board shall have power to purchase , Rights have , hold , secure , enjoy , possess and retain to itself , in perpetuity or for any term of years , any land , tenements or hereditaments , or any other property of any nature what- soever , not exceeding the sum of five hundred thousand dol- lars , or to sell or alien the same , as the Board may see fit ; and by its said name to sue and be sued , plead and be im- pleaded , in any Court of competent jurisdiction in this State , and to make such rules and by - laws for its own gov- ernment as are not repugnant to the laws of the land , and for the order , good government and management thereof , as may be thought necessary and expedient : Provided , That nothing herein contained shall be construed to authorize the said Board to remove the institution under its direction from the town of Clinton , in Laurens County , without the unanimous consent of the Pastor , Elders and Deacons duly appointed from the Clinton Presbyterian Church . The said Board is authorized hereby to maintain such school or schools of a collegiate , normal and technical character as may be found necessary , and may , under the name of the Thornwell Seminary for Orphans , the Thornwell Mission Training College and the Thornwell Technical Institute , con- fer such diplomas and degrees as are usual in colleges . That the said Board is prohibited from accepting the guardian- ship of any child in the institution , either its person or prop- erty , except that it may refuse to surrender orphans to any but legally appointed guardians or their surviving parent when its protection is sought by any of its orphans .

Sec . 3. That this Act shall be deemed a public Act and continue in force until repealed .


Year:1894       ACT NO.:663
"AN ACT TO AMEND AN ACT ENTITLED ""AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A NEW SCHOOL DISTRICT IN YORK COUNTY AND TO AUTHORIZE THE LEVY
AND COLLECTION OF A LOCAL TAX THEREIN,"" APPROVED DECEMBER 23D, 1887 , BY STRIKING OUT SECTION 5 AND INSERTING A NEW SECTION IN LIEU THEREOF, AS
TO THE ELECTION AND TENURE AND POWERS OF TRUSTEES , AND TO REPEAL INCONSISTENT ACTS AND PARTS OF ACTS ."

Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the State of South Carolina , now met and sitting in Gen- eral Assembly , and by the authority of the same , That Sec- tion 5 of an Act entitled " An Act to provide for the estab- lishment of a new school district in York County and to authorize the levy and collection of a local tax therein , " approved December 23d , 1887 , be , and the same is hereby , amended by striking out all of Section 5 of said Act and in- serting in lieu thereof the following in the said Act , to be known as Section 5 thereof :

Section 5. That three Trustees for said Graded School District of Blacksburg , S. C. , shall be elected ; that the said election shall be held on the first Tuesday in February , 1894 , and on the first Tuesday in February of each and every year thereafter in the said town , the polls to be opened at 1 o'clock P. M. and closed at 5 o'clock P. M .; that the Town Council of Blacksburg , S. C. , shall appoint the Managers of said election , who shall be sworn as Managers of other elec- tions are sworn . The said Managers shall conduct the elec- tion as other elections are conducted , count the votes and declare the result . The three persons receiving the greatest number of votes cast at said election shall be declared elected , and upon taking the oath of office , as required by Powers of the Constitution , shall be clothed with all the powers and authority within said district that other Trustees exercise under the general law , and shall also have within said dis- trict the authority confirmed by this Act . Any resident of the said school district qualified to vote for members of the General Assembly at the general election shall be eligible to vote at the elections to be held under provisions of this Act . Trustees elected hereunder shall serve until their suc- cessors are elected and qualified , and the Board of Trustees shall have power to fill any vacancy occurring between elec- tions , whether by death , resignation , removal or otherwise , Repealing and that all Acts and parts of Acts inconsistent with this Act and referring thereto are hereby repealed.


Year:1894       ACT NO.:670
AN ACT TO REVISE AND RE-ENACT THE CHARTER OF THE
TOWN OF GAFFNEY CITY, IN SPARTANBURG COUNTY .

Section 1. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Rep- resentatives of the State of South Carolina, now met and sit- ting in General Assembly, and by the authority of the same, That from and after the passage of this Act all citizens of this State having resided twelve months within the State and six months within the town of Gaffney City shall be deemed, and are hereby declared to be, a body politic and corporate, and the said town shall be known and called by the name of Gaffney City, and its corporate limits shall ex- tend one (1) mile in every direction from the centre of said town, which centre shall be at the intersection of Race and Johnson streets. 

Sec. 2. That the municipal powers of the town of Gaffney City shall be, and they are hereby, vested in an Intendant and four Wardens of said town, which shall be and be known as the Town Council of said town, and who shall be persons constitutionally qualified to vote for members of the General Assembly of this State, and who shall have resided within the corporate limits of the said town for twelve months next preceding election to said office. 

Sec. 3. That the election for the Intendant and Wardens of said town shall be holden on the first Tuesday in March, 1896, and on the same day every two (2) years thereafter, ten days’ public notice thereof being previously given; and the said officers elected shall continue in office for two years and until the election and qualification of their successors; and all male inhabitants within said town who shall have attained the age of twenty-one (21) years, and resided in the said State and town of Gaffney City for twelve (12) months immediately preceding the election, and who are qualified to vote in the State elections, shall be entitled to vote for said Intendant and Wardens. It shall be the duty of the Intendant and Wardens of said town to require a registra- tion of all voters of said town as a prerequisite to voting at any election for Intendant and Wardens thereof, and for this purpose full power is hereby vested in the Town Coun- cil of said town to prescribe the time, place, manner and terms of said registration of voters by an ordinance for that purpose. That the said election shall be held in some con- venient place in said town, from nine (9) o’clock in the morn- ing until three (3) o’clock in the afternoon, when the polls shall be closed and the Managers shall forthwith count the votes and declare the election, and give notice in writing to the persons elected. The Intendant and Wardens for the time being shall appoint three Managers to conduct the election, who, before they open the polls for the said elec- tion, shall take an oath fairly and impartially to conduct the same. The Intendant and Wardens, before entering upon the duties of their office, shall respectively take the oath prescribed by the Constitution of the State, and also the fol- lowing oath, to wit: “As Intendant (or Warden) of the town of Gaffney City, I will equally and impartially, to the best of my ability, execute the trust imposed in me, and will use my best endeavors to preserve.the peace and carry into effect, according to law, the purposes for which I have been elected, so help me God.” And if any person upon being elected Intendant or Warden shall refuse to act as such, he shall forfeit and pay the said Town Council the sum of twenty-five dollars for the use of said town: Provided, That no person who has attained the age of sixty (60) years shall be compelled to serve in either of said offices, nor shall any other person be compelled to serve, either as Intendant or Warden, more than one term in succession: Provided, That the present Intendant and Wardens of said town shall hold their offices for the term to which they were elected, that is to say, until the first Tuesday in March, A. D. 1896, and until their successors shall be elected and qualified as herein provided for. 

Sec. 4. That if for any reason the election hereinbefore provided for shall fail to be held at the time appointed therefor, it shall be the duty of the Intendant and Wardens of the said town to order an election to be held as soon as practicable thereafter, ten days’ public notice thereof being previously given. 

Sec. 5. That said Intendant and Wardens are empowered to pass all ordinances, rules and regulations for the fair and just management of said elections, and to prevent any fraud- ulent voting thereat, and to punish all offenses against the same by fine not exceeding fifty dollars or imprisonment not exceeding thirty days. 

Sec. 6. That the Intendant and two Wardens, or, in the absence of the Intendant, three Wardens, shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business; and in case a vacancy shall occur in the office of Intendant or Warden by death, resignation, removal, or for any other cause, an elec- tion to fill such vacancy shall be held by order of the Intend- ant, or Intendant pro tem., ten days’ public notice being previously given, which election shall be conducted in all respects and be subject to all the regulations hereinafter provided for the regular elections; and in case of sickness, temporary absence or disability of the Intendant, the Ward- ens shall be empowered to elect one of their number to act as Intendant pro tem. 

Sec. 7 That the Intendant and Wardens shall be known as the “Town Council of Gaffney City, S. C.,” and they and their successors in office, hereafter to be elected, may have a common seal, which shall be affixed to all their ordinances; may sue and be sued, plead and be impleaded, in any Court of law or equity in this State, and purchase, hold, possess and enjoy, to them and their successors, in perpetuity or for any term of years, any estate, real, personal or mixed, and sell, alien, convey and Jease the same: Provided, The same shall not exceed at any one time the sum of one hundred thousand dollars. And the said Town Council shall have full power and authority to establish or authorize the estab- lishment of a market house in the said town, and to pre- scribe suitable rules and regulations for the same; and to establish or authorize the establishment of a guard house and to prescribe suitable rules and regulations for keeping and governing the same; and the said Town Council shall have full power and authority, under their corporate seal, to make all such rules, by-laws and ordinances respecting the streets, roads, parks, drainage, market houses and the business thereof, buildings, trade and police system of said town, as shal] appear to them necessary and proper for the security, welfare and convenience of the said town, and for preserving health, peace, order and good government and morals within the same, and for the protection of life and property within said town; and said Town Council shall have full power and authority to abate and remove all nui- sances in the said town. 

Sec. 8. That said Intendant, Intendant pro tem., or Town Council, may fine and impose fines and penalties and im- prisonment in the guard house of the town for violation of the ordinances and by-laws of said town; said fines, penal- ties and imprisonment to be imposed singly or in the alter- native; but no fine or penalty to exceed the sum of one hun- dred dollars, and no term of imprisonment to exceed thirty (30) days; and they shall appropriate all fines to the public use of the said corporation. 

Sec. 9. That the said Intendant or Town Council, or both of them, are hereby vested with all the powers and jurisdic- tion of Trial Justices in this State within the limits of said town, so far as the violation of municipal ordinances are concerned, and except for the trial of civil cases. The said Intendant, or Intendant pro tem., shall have power to try all offenders against the ordinances and by-laws of the said town immediately upon their apprehension, arrest, or as soon thereafter as practicable, unless such persons enter into a good and sufficient bond, to be approved by the In- tendant, or, in his absence, by the Clerk of the Town Coun- cil, or make satisfactory money deposit, to appear for trial at a time fixed not later than five days after the arrest of said person or persons, in which event the trial shall be deferred until that time; and the said Intendant or Town Council, or both of them, shall have the same power which Trial Justices now have, or shall hereafter be vested with, to compel the attendance of witnesses, wherever they may reside, and within the jurisdiction of the Trial Justices of the County, the same as in prosecutions for criminal offenses in said Trial Justice Court, and require them to give evi- dence upon the trial before him or them of any person or persons for a violation of any of the ordinances or by-laws of the said Town Council; and in the trial of all offenders against the ordinances or by-laws of said town, the Intend- ant or Town Council shall be governed by the same rules shall of procedure and evidence as are now or hereafter be prescribed for the government of Courts of Trial Justices in criminal cases: Provided, That the same right of appeal shall be allowed as in cases of ap- peal from Courts of Trial Justices in this State. Whenever the Intendant shall find any person before him guilty of violating an ordinance or by-law of said town, he shall have power to impose, in his discretion, fine or imprisonment within the limits herein prescribed for such violations: Pro- vided, That whenever the Intendant, Intendant pro tem., or Town Council, shall impose a fine upon a person convicted of an offense who shall fail, refuse or be unable to pay the same, said Intendant or Town Council shall have the power and authority to commute the sentence of said person to that of labor on the public streets or public improvements of said town for a term not exceeding thirty (80) days. From all trials, sentences and decisions of the said Intendant, any person feeling aggrieved shall have the right to appeal to the Town Council: Provided, Written notice of such appeal be immediately given to the Intendant upon such sentence being pronounced, and said person entering into a bond to appear and defend before the Town Council at a time to be specified in such undertaking, not more than ten (10) days after the date of such bond. 

Sec. 10. In any case tried under the foregoing Section, upon appeal to the full Council, the trial shall proceed de novo, and the Intendant and three Wardens, or, in the absence or inability of the Intendant to serve, the four Wardens, shall be sufficient to proceed with the trial of such cause or appeal, and a decision of a majority of those pres- ent shall determine all questions before the said Council, except the questions of fact involved, in which the Intend- ant who tried the case shall have no vote, but shall be deter- mined by a majority of the Wardens trying the case: Pro- vided, That in case of a tie vote of the Wardens on the facts involved, the Intendant shall have the casting vote, and the decision of the majority as thus ascertained shall determine the case and be final: Provided, further, That the Intend- ant, Intendant pro tem., or Town Council, shall have power to enforce the observance of order and decorum in their Municipal Court while any trial is being held, and for said purpose said Intendant or Town Council is hereby vested with full power to punish as for a contempt any person who shall, in the presence of said Court, offer an insult to said Intendant or to any one of the Wardens, or who shall be considered by the Court guilty of a disturbance of the pro- ceedings in said Court, by fine not exceeding twenty dollars, or imprisonment in the guard house not exceeding ten days, for each and every offense. 

Sec. 11. The Intendant shall have authority to summon the Council to meet for the transaction of business pertain- ing to the corporation whenever in his judgment it may be necessary. Sec. 12. The Town Council of said town shall have full power and authority to purchase and operate, rent or lease, under such rules, regulations and orders as they may by ordinance adopt, water and electric works, in or near said town, for the use and benefit of said town and its citizens; also, to purchase, own and operate, rent or lease, apparatus for generating either electricity or gas for the use,and bene- fit of said town and its citizens, or to contract for the erec- tion of plants, either for water works or lighting purposes, one or both, for the uses of said town and to supply the citizens thereof, to grant a franchise or franchises for said purposes, as well as for the construction and operation of a street railway within said town, to any private corporation or corporations for a term of years as may be deemed to be to the best interest of said town, with power to make such by-laws, rules and ordinances in reference thereto as shall be deemed necessary for the regulation and proper conduct of the same, either for public or private use by the citizens of said town: Provided, That no such franchise shall be granted until the question of granting thereof has first been submitted to the qualified voters of said town and approved by the majority of such persons voting at such election. 

Sec. 13. The Intendant and Wardens shall have full and exclusive control over all streets, roads, ways and bridges in the said town, and it shall be their duty to keep them open and in good repair; and for that purpose they are invested with all the powers of County Board of Commissioners for and‘ within the coporate limits of said town, and they shall have power to classify and arrange the inhabitants or citi- zens of said town liable to street, road or public duty therein, and to enforce the performance of such duty under such penalties, rules and regulations as shall be provided for by the ordinances of said town; and they shall have power to compound with all persons liable to work the streets, ways and roads in said town, upon such terms as their ordinances or by-laws may establish or their rules and regulations re- quire, the money so received to be applied to the public use of said corporation; and all persons refusing to labor or fail- ing to pay such commutation shall be liable to such fine, not exceeding ten dollars, or imprisonment, not exceeding twenty days, as the said Town Council may impose; and they shall have power to enforce the payment of such. fine or to impose such imprisonment as in all other cases for violation of ordinances. 

Sec. 14. The Town Council of Gaffney City shall have full power and authority to open new streets in said town, and to close up, widen or otherwise alter those now in use, or which may hereafter be established, wheresoever, in their judgment, the same may be necessary for the improvement and convenience of said town, and to name and change pres- ent names of streets. Should the land owner or owners through whose premises such street or streets may run re fuse his, her or their consent to such action of the Town Council in opening, closing up, widening or altering such street or streets, the said Town Council shall have the right to condemn such land for the purpose aforesaid, according to the provisions of the law now of force for condemning land for public use. 

Sec. 15. The cemeteries and public graveyards are also placed under the jurisdiction of the said Town Council. 

Sec. 16. That said Town Council shall have the right, either independently of or in connection with any associa- tion of the citizens of said town, to establish and maintain, or to assist in establishing and maintaining, a public library for the use and benefit of the citizens of said town, under such rules and regulations as they may by ordinances adopt. 

Sec. 17. That the said Town Council shall have full power and authority to prohibit, by suitable penalties, the erection of any wooden building or buildings within such limits in the said town as the Town Council shall designate by an ordinance or ordinances fur such purpose, duly passed and ratified by the said Town Council, not inconsistent with the Constitution and laws of this State, and published one time in a newspaper published in said town, or by posting the same for one week in a conspicuous place in said town. 

Sec. 18. The said Town Council shall have full power to regulate sales at auction within the corporate limits of said town, and to grant licenses to auctioneers, itinerants, traders and keepers of hotels and livery, sale or exchange stables, and to persons who sell fresh or uncured pork, fish or other fresh meats within the corporate limits of said town, upon such terms and condtitions, and subject to such regulations, as said Council may by ordinance establish: Provided, That nothing herein contained shall extend to sales by Sheriffs, executors or administrators, or by any other person, under the order of any Court; and the said Town Council shall have the power to impose a tax on all drays, carts, wagons, carriages, omnibuses, buggies, horses, mares or mules kept for hire or used for public purposes in said town, and upon every tenpin alley, pool, billiard, baga- telle or other table of any kind or name upon which games are played for gain or reward, within the corporate limits of said town; and to require all persons owning or keeping a dog or dogs within said town to pay an annual license tax not exceeding two dollars for each dog so owned or kept, and to enforce and regulate the payment of said license tax under such rules and regulations as said Town Council may deem proper, to charge and collect in advance a license tax upon every show or exhibition for gain or reward within the corporate limits of said town; and said Town Council shall have full power to grant or refuse licenses for retailing in- toxicating liquors, wines or malt liquors, subject, however, to the laws of the State, and when not in conflict therewith. 

Sec. 19. The said Town Council shall be authorized and empowered to require all persons, companies and corporations now engaged, or who may hereafter become engaged, in any business vocation, trade or profession of any kind whatsoever within the limits of said town, and all transient persons, companies or corporations engaged in or about to engage in any business in said town, to take out a license from the Town Council, who shall be authorized to impose such charges or license tax for the conduct of the same as by ordinance of the said town may be provided; and the revenue derived from such license or tax shall be for the public use of said town, and the Town Council may enforce the payment of such license or tax in such manner as they may by ordinance provide. 

Sec. 20. The said Town Council shall have the power to impose an annual tax not exceeding eighty (80) cents on every hundred dollars of the value of all real estate and per- sonal property lying within the corporate limits of said town, real and personal property of churches, cemeteries, schools, colleges, associations and public libraries excepted. An ordinance declaring the rate of the annual taxation for the year shall be published or posted at least two (2) weeks during the month of January in each year. All persons liable to taxation in said town shall, during the month of January, make return, under oath, to the Clerk of said Town Council, or to some other person appointed for said purpose, of their taxable property within said town, in the same man- ner as is required by law for the return of property for tax- ation for State and County taxes; and the said Town Council shall appoint three discreet freeholders, residents of said town, who, upon taking the oath prescribed for officers in the Constitution, shall meet during the last week in Jan- uary and the first week in February and elect a Chairman, and when so organized shall form a Board of Assessors for said town, with full power to review the said returns of property made by taxpayers, with power to alter the same with the view of assessing all property, both real and per- sonal, at its true value, and of equalizing the assessment of said property, and to assess all property for taxation not so returned, and their assessment so made shall be reported to the Town Council and shall be taken as the true value thereof for the purposes of taxation in said town: Provided, That the taxpayers shall have ten days thereafter in which to make complaint of such assessment to the Town Council; and upon good cause shown, the Town Council may alter any assessment. Payment of said taxes shall be made to the Clerk of said Town Council, or to such other person as may be authorized to colléct and receive the same, during the month of February after the publication, and until the first Tuesday in March thereafter; and upon failure to make such return and payment, or either, as herein required, the person so in default shall be subject to the penalties pro- vided by law for failure to make return and pay the general State and County tax, to be enforced by the order of the Intendant and Wardens, or a majority of them, for the use of the said town, except that in such cases executions to enforce the payment of such taxes shall be issued under the seal of the corporation, and may be directed to the Chief of Police or other person appointed by the Town Council to levy, collect and receive the same, with costs, as in such eases made and provided by law; and all property upon which such tax shall be levied and assessed is hereby de- clared and made liable for payment thereof in preference to all other debts, except debts due to the State and County, which shall be first paid; and all other taxes imposed by the Intendant and Wardens, or a majority of them, shall be enforced and collected as in manner and form just before stated: Provided, That said Town Council shall have full power to levy and collect a tax for the year 1895 under the same rules, regulations and provisions as set forth in this Section. 

Sec. 21. That said Town Council shall have full power and authority to abate all nuisances within, or partly within, the corporate limits of said town, and also to appoint a Board of Health for said town, and to pass such ordinances as may be necessary to define the duties and powers of said Board of Health, and to impose a fine of not more than twenty-five dollars upon any person who shall refuse to serve upon said Board of Health; and it is expressly pro- vided that upon the failure of any person in possession of land, lot or house, within the corporate limits of said town, to cleanse the privies or water closets, or remove any other nuisance from the premises in his or her possession, or under his or her control, when so directed to do by either the Town Council or the Board of Health, it shall be the duty of the said Town Council to cause their Marshal or other employees to enter the premises in question and to abate said nuisance at the expense of the person in possession of said premises; and said Town Council shall have power to pro- vide by ordinance for the punishment of any and all per- sons who shall interfere with the Marshals in the discharge of the duties imposed on them in said ordinance, or who shall fail or refuse to pay the expenses of abating the nui- sance upon the demand of the same by the Town Council. 

See. 22. That the said Town Council shall have power, and are hereby authorized, to elect one Chief of Police and as many assistants as may be necessary, to fix their salaries and prescribe their duties. They shall be sworn in and vested with all the powers now conferred by law upon Con- stables, and subject to all the duties and liabilities that are now or may hereafter be conferred upon Constables, in addition to the special duties devolved upon them by the Town Council: Provided, That their jurisdiction shall not extend beyond the limits of the said corporation; that the Intendant shall have power to suspend, dismiss or discharge from office any town Marshal or policeman for neglect of duty or improper conduct in the discharge of his official duties, subject, however, to the approval of the Wardens or a majority thereof; and said Council shall have the power to elect a Town Clerk and Treasurer, whose duties shall be prescribed by them, and they shall also fix said Town Clerk’s salary, which shall not be less than two bun- dred dollars per annum, and require him and the Treasurer to enter into a bond, to be approved by the Intendant, con- ditioned upon the faithful performance of the duties of their oftice. Said bond not to be for a less sum than two thou- sand ($2,000) dollars each. 

See. 23. The said Town Council shall have the power by ordinance, or the Intendant and Wardens in person, any one or more of them, to authorize and direct any policeman of said town to arrest and commit to the guard house of the town for a term not exceeding twenty-four (24) hours before trial, unless such arrest be made on Saturday, in which case it shall not exceed forty-eight (48) hours before trial, any person or persons who, within the said corporate limits, may be engaged in any breach of the peace, riotous or disorderly conduct, open obscenity, public drunkenness, or in any conduct grossly indecent or dangerous to the citizens of the said town or any of them; and it shall be the duty of any Marshal or policeman of said town to arrest and commit all such offenders, when required by said ordinances, or by any member of the Town Council, so to do; and they shall have power to call to their assistance the posse comitatus, if need be, in making such arrest; and upon failure of such Marshal or policeman to perform their duty as required, they shall severally be liable to such fines and penalties as said Town Council may establish; and all persons so im- prisoned shall pay the costs and expenses incident to such imprisonment, which said costs and expenses shall be col- lected in the same manner as is provided for the collection of fines imposed for the violation of the town ordinances: Provided, That the imprisonment provided for in this Sec- tion shall not exempt the person so imprisoned from trial and sentence, as hereinbefore provided. 

Sec. 24. That the said Town Council shall have full power to erect a powder magazine, and to compel every person holding more than one hundred pounds of powder at any one time to store the same therein, and to make regulations for rates of storage therein. They shall also have power to prohibit absolutely the keeping of dynamite in any quantity whatsoever within the corporate limits of said town, except as permitted by the Town Council for special purpose in said town by ordinance. That the said Town Council is hereby authorized and empowered to establish and keep up one or more public scales for weighing cotton and other articles sold by weight in said town, and to appoint one or more public weighers, who shall give good bond, to be approved by the Intendant, and who shall be sworn by said Intendant faithfully to perform the duties of said office, and who shall be removable for misconduct or incompetency by the said Town Council; and the said Town Council are hereby au- thorized to assess a sum not exceeding ten (10) cents on each bale of cotton, and a proportionate sum on other articles weighed, to be paid by the seller or buyer, as may be agreed upon between them, for the use of said town. That the pub- lic scales established in pursuance of this Act shall be the standard to which all others in said town shall conform; and the Town Council may establish by ordinance such rules and regulations as may be deemed necessary to effectually carry out the provisions of this Section. 

Sec. 25. That the Intendant of said town shall receive as a salary for his services a sum to be fixed by the Town Council, not less than three hundred dollars per annum. He and the Wardens and their Marshals shall each be exempt from street and jury duty within said town during their term of office, and each Town Council shall, within thirty days after the expiration of their term of office, make out and return to their successors a full account of their re- ceipts and expenditures during their term of office. And at the expiration of the term of office of each Town Council it shall be their duty to pay over to their successors any moneys in their hands, at the time of making such returns, belonging to said corporation, and likewise to deliver up promptly, at the end of each Town Council term, all books, records, property and papers incident to their said oflice to their successors; and on failure so to do they shall be liable to be fined in a sum of five hundred dollars, to be col- lected by said Town Council by suit in any Court of com- petent jurisdiction. 

Sec. 26. The said Town Council shall have power and authority to close in all the lots in said town, and to make and keep in good repair, by paving or otherwise, all side- walks in front of any lot or lots whereon the same shall front or adjoin any public street of the said town, if, in the judgment of the Council, such sidewalks shall be necessary, the width thereof and the manner of construction to be designated and regulated by the Town Council, and to re- quire the owner or owners to pay the price of making or re- pairing; and the said town shall have a lien in preference to all other liens for said work performed and material used on the property benefited by said improvements; and the said Town Council is hereby empowered to sue for and re- cover the same by action of debt in any Court of competent jurisdiction: Provided, That such owner or owners shall not be required to pay more than the actual cost of such im- provements. That said Town Council shall have the power to elect or appoint a civil engineer for said town, whose duties shall be prescribed by an ordinance duly passed for that purpose. 

Sec. 27. For any willful violation or neglect of duty, mal- practice, abuse or oppression, the Intendant or any Warden so offending shall be liable to punishment by fine not exceeding one hundred dollars, or imprisonment not exceed- ing thirty days, besides being liable for damages to any per- son injured by such neglect, malpractice, abuse or oppres- sion. 

Sec. 28. Any person who shall receive bodily injury or damages in his person or property through a defect in any street, causeway, bridge, or public way, or by reason of de- fect or mismanagement of anything under the control of the corporation within the limits of said town may recover in an action against the same the amount of actual damages sustained by him or her by reason thereof. If any such de- fect in a street, causeway or bridge existed before such in- jury or damage occurred, such damage shall not be recov- ered by the person so injured if his load exceeded the ordi- nary weight: Provided, That said corporation shall not be liable unless said defect was occasioned by its neglect or mismanagement: Provided, further, Such person has not, in any way, brought about such injury or damage by his or her own negligent act or negligently contributed thereto. 

Sec. 29. That this Act shall go into effect immediately upon its approval, and all ordinances, by-laws, rules and regulations which are now in force in said town of Gaffney City, and all contracts and all acts done by the Town Coun- cil of Gaffney City, shall continue and be of force to the same extent, tenor and effect as now exists, and nothing herein shall be deemed or taken in any way to impair any such rules, regulations, ordinances and contracts of the said town. 

Sec. 30. That all Acts or parts of Acts heretofore passed relating to or bearing upon the incorporation of the town of Gaffney City and inconsistent with and repugnant to this Act be, and the same are hereby, repealed. 

Sec. 31. That this Act shall be deemed and taken to be a public Act, and shall continue in force until repealed.

Year:1894       ACT NO.:700
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE TOWN COUNCIL OF BARNWELL TO ISSUE BONDS FOR THE PURPOSE OF PAYING PAST IN- DEBTEDNESS AND EQUIPPING THE OPERA HOUSE AND TO PROVIDE FOR THE INTEREST ACCRUING THEREON .

Section 1. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Rep- resentatives of the State of South Carolina, now met and sit- ting in General Assembly, and by the authority of the same, 

That the Town Council of Barnwell shall have power, and are hereby authorized, to issue bonds of said town, on or before the first day of February, 1895, to the amount of two thousand and five hundred dollars, for the purpose of pay- ing off the judgment against said town and completing and equipping the Opera House, said bonds to be issued in such denomination as said Town Council may deem best, and to be made payable twenty years from the date of said bonds, with interest payable semi-annually at the rate of not more than eight per cent. per annum, and the coupons for said interest, when due, to be receivable in payments of all taxes levied by or due to said town. 
Sec. 2. That the money arising from the said bonds be used exclusively for the purposes set out in Section 1 of this Act, and to this end shall be expended under the direction and control of the said Town Council. 
Sec. 3. That the said Town Council shall semi-annually, at such time and place as they shall fix and determine, pay the interest due on said bonds, and for this purpose the said Town Council, in addition to the powers already conferred, shall be, and they hereby are, authorized and required to levy such tax upon the real and personal property assessed for taxation in the said town as may be deemed necessary to pay the interest on said bonds which may become due in each and every year, until the whole of said bonds be paid. 
Sec. 4. All Acts and parts of Acts inconsistent with the provisions of this Act be, and the same are hereby, repealed. Sec. 5. That this Act shall take effect immediately after its approval by the Governor.

Section 1. Sec . 2. That the said district shall be known as the Water- loo School District , and shall be a , body politic and cor- porate , with such government , rights , privileges and lia- bilities as are provided for school districts by the School 20 Stat . , 49. Law of South Carolina , approved December 24th , A. D. 1888 . Sec . 3. That , in addition to the rights and privileges here- inbefore granted , the said school district shall have power to levy on all real and personal property returned in said district a tax not exceeding three mills on the dollar , subject A. D. 1894 . to the following provisions : The School Trustees of said school district shall , at any time previous to the 30th day of January of each fiscal year , upon the written request of twenty property holders , issue a call for a public meeting Meeting of ( after two weeks ' notice ) of all those citizens who return real or personal property in said district , and said notice shall be published in at least one newspaper , and posted in two conspicuous places in said district , for at least two weeks before such meeting , and shall specify the time , place and object of said meeting .

Sec . 4. That when the persons answering the above de- scription shall have assembled in public meeting they shall have power : First . To select a Chairman and secretary , Proceeding at adjourn from time to time , decide what additional tax , if any , shall be levied , and appropriate the same in such man- ner as they may think best for the educational interest of said school district : Provided , That no tax thus levied shall be repealed at a subsequent meeting in the same fiscal year . Second . To elect and dismiss superintendents and teachers of the Teachers . schools , prescribe the duties , terms of office , and to fix their salaries , and to cause an examination of said teachers to be made whenever necessary ; also to determine the class books and studies to be used in the said schools , and to make rules and regulations for the government of said schools . 3. To Expenditure determine the manner in which the tax heretofore author- ized ( and the two mills Constitutional and poll tax provided by law ) shall be expended in maintaining said public schools ; and 4. To fill all vacancies occurring in said Board of Trus- Vacancies . tees by death , resignation , removal or otherwise during their term of office or service .

Sec . 5. Sec . 7. That Col. J. H. Wharton , D. C. Smith , B. A. Ander- son , Prof. W. T. McElroy , Joseph Pearce , H. C. Fuller and T. N. Parks are hereby authorized and required to act until the election of the Trustees provided for in this Act .

Year:1894       ACT NO.:752
AN ACT TO EXEMPT CERTAIN PORTIONS OF KERSHAW COUNTY FROM THE OPERATION OF THE PROVISIONS OF CHAPTER XXV. OF THE REVISED STATUTES , RELATING TO THE STOCK LAW. 

Section 1. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Rep- resentatives of the State of South Carolina, now met and sit- ting in General Assembly, and by the authority of the same, That all that certain section of the County of Kershaw lying within the following boundaries, to wit: The right of way of the Charleston, Cincinnati and Chicago Railroad Com- pany, commencing at the five-mile post from Camden, thence to Hanging Rock Creek to Lynch’s River; thence along said river to a point where it is crossed by the public road be- tween Camden and Cheraw, known as the Telegraph Wire road; thence along said road to the five-mile post from Camden, thence to the starting point, be, and the same is hereby, exempted from the operations of the provisions of Chapter XAYV. of the Revised Statutes of the State, known as the Stock Law: Provided, That the residents of the section named shall build a good and sufficient fence along the lines above described to protect the lands outside of said territory from incursions of all stock and animals named in said Gen- eral Stock Law; and this exemption shall not take effect until the said fence is completed, and shall cease as soon as there is a failure to keep up said fence at any point: Pro- vided, further, That good, convenient and substantial gates shall be placed on all public roads crossed by this fence, and the penalty for leaving them open shall be the same as for leaving pasture fences down, as provided for in the General Stock Law: Provided, further, That any landholder whose lands are on the lines herein set forth may have his or her lands excluded from the provisions of this Act by requiring the County Commissioners of said County to locate the boundary line or lines so as to leave his or her lands with- out the territory embraced within the boundary lines set forth in this Act: Provided, further, That said fence be com- pleted on or before the first day of March, 1896; and in case of failure to complete the fence by said time, then this Act shall not apply. 

Sec. 2. That the County Supervisor of Kershaw County shall, and he is hereby, authorized and directed to determine the exact location of the aforesaid boundary lines: Pro- vided, That the General Stock Law as it now exists shall apply to all stock not kept within the lines prescribed in this Act. 

Sec. 3. That all Acts and parts of Acts inconsistent with this Act be, and the same are hereby, repealed. Approved

"AN ACT TO AMEND AN ACT ENTITLED ""AN ACT TO AMEND THE CHARTER OF THE TOWN OF SUMMERVILLE,""APPROVED DECEMBER 22ND , A. D. 1885 ."

Section 1. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Rep- resentatives of the State of South Carolina , now met and sit- ting in General Assembly , and by the authority of the same , That Section 2 of an Act entitled " An Act to amend the charter of the town of Summerville " be , and the same is hereby , amended so that said Section when so amended shall read as follows :
Section 2. The said town shall be governed by an Intend- ant and six ( 6 ) Wardens , who shall be citizens of the State , twenty - one ( 21 ) years of age , and shall have resided at least twelve ( 12 ) months within the corporate limits of the town immediately preceding the day of their election . The said Intendant and Wardens shall be known and called the " Town Council of Summerville , " and shall be elected at the same time on the second ( 2d ) Wednesday in July of every second year , and shall hold office for the term of two years , and until their successors shall have been duly elected and qualified . The next election shall take place on the second Next election . Wednesday in July , A. D. 1895 , and the present Intendant and Wardens and other officers shall hold office until their successors are elected and qualified . The Intendant and three ( 3 ) of the Wardens , or any four ( 4 ) of the Wardens , shall constitute a quorum for the purpose of transacting business or exercising the powers herein granted to the " Town Council of Summerville , " or the said Intendant and Wardens .
Sec . 3. That Section 4 of said Act be , and the same hereby is , amended so that said Section when so amended shall read as follows :

Section 4. For the purpose of conducting the elections for members of the Town Council , it shall be the duty of the Governor , at least sixty ( 60 ) days before the next elec- tion , and at least sixty ( 60 ) days before each succeeding appoint Com- election , to appoint three ( 3 ) electors , who shall constitute a Board of Commissioners of Election for the town of Sum- merville , who shall hold their office , unless removed by the Governor , until sixty ( 60 ) days before the next election for members of the Town Council of said town , and until their successors are duly appointed and qualified . The Commis- sioners of Election shall appoint three ( 3 ) Managers of Elec- tion , who shall on the first Wednesday in May immediately preceding the second Wednesday in July appointed for hold- ing such election , for two consecutive days , at or near the depot of the South Carolina and Georgia Railroad Company , open lists for the registration of the qualified voters of the town who are not entitled to vote upon a property qualifica- tion , between the hours of seven A. M. and twelve M. , and again between the hours of three P. M. and six P. M. The after taking the oath of office prescribed by the Consti- tution of the State , Section 30 , Article II . , before any person qualified to administer an oath , shall administer the same to the two other Managers . The Managers shall administer to every person offering to register the following oath : " You do solemnly swear that you are duly qualified to vote Oath for regis- for members of the Legislature of the State of South Caro- lina , and that you have resided within the corporate limits of this town for the four months last past , and that it is your intention to continue to reside within the corporate limits until the day for holding the ensuing election , and that you have truly stated your name and place of residence ; so help you God . " Upon the Managers being satisfied of such per- son's right to register , they shall duly register his name and place of residence , and issue to him a certificate of his regis- tration , which certificate shall state the name of the voter , the date of registration , his place of residence , and shall be signed by the Chairman of the Board of Managers and by their Clerk . The registration list , when completed , shall List . be duly sealed up and delivered by the said Managers to the Commissioners of Election , together with all books and papers that may pertain to such registration , and the same shall be kept by the said Commissioners , unopened , and shall be so returned to the said Managers on the day of the said election .

Section 5. M. , and keep the same open until 6 P. M. Every person entitled to vote upon a property qualification as set forth in Section 3 of this Act shall be allowed to vote upon taking the following oath : " I do solemnly swear Oath for voter . that I am duly qualified to vote at this election for the mem- bers ( or member , as the case may be , ) of the Town Council of Summerville ; so help me God . " If any person's right to vote on a property qualification is denied , the Managers shall require some evidence of his title to the property giv ing the qualification . Section 8. Said election to be conducted under the regulations hereinbefore provided for the regular election of members of the Town Council .

In case a vacancy occurs in the office of any one or more of the Wardens , by death , resignation or otherwise , the va- cancy or vacancies shall be filled by the remaining mem- bers of the Town Council .

Sec . 6. That the Town Council of the town of Summer- ville , in this State , be , and the same is hereby , authorized , Encroachments in cases where any person or persons have encroached by remedied . means of buildings , fences or other structures upon the streets or roads or premises claimed to be part and parcel of the streets or roads of the said town , in its discretion , to treat and arrange with said party or parties in regard to the same , with power to agree that the portion encroached upon or any part thereof shall be and become the property of the encroaching party or parties , upon such terms and for such considerations as may be mutually agreed upon ; and also in its discretion to arrange with any such party or par- ties for the proper location of the line and lines between the streets aforesaid and private property , and on such arrange- ments being made , and said lines duly established , the same shall be the true lines , notwithstanding that what was or was claimed to be a part of any street may thus become a part of private premises : Provided , however , That in any Proviso . and all cases where no such arrangement shall be proposed or completed , and until any such arrangement shall be agreed upon and completed , nothing herein contained shall be construed to prejudice the State , or any person or per- sons , or the said Town Council , in respect to any and all rights and remedies and the exercise thereof regarding ob- structions of or encroachments upon the streets or roads of the said town .


Year:1894       ACT NO.:761
AN ACT TO INCORPORATE THE CITY OF ABBEVILLE .

Section 1. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Rep- resentatives of the State of South Carolina , now met and sit- ting in General Assembly , and by the authority of the same , That from and after the passage of this Act all persons who shall have been domiciled in this State one year , and who may have resided within the corporate limits of the town of Abbeville sixty days , and their successors , are hereby de- Creation , name clared to be a body politic and corporate , under the name of the city of Abbeville , and the corporate limits of the said city shall extend one mile and a quarter in every direction from the court house in said town as a centre .

Sec . 2. That the said city is hereby divided into four wards , as follows : The territory lying between a line drawn along the centre of Main street on the Southwest and a line drawn along the centre of Washington and Cambridge streets on the Southeast shall be known as Ward One ; the territory lying between a line drawn along the centre of Washington and Cambridge streets on the Northwest and a line drawn along the centre of Main street on the Southwest shall be known as Ward Two ; the territory lying between a line drawn along the centre of Main street on the Northeast and a line drawn along the centre of Pinckney and Ferry streets on the Northwest shall be known as Ward Three ; the terri- tory lying between a line drawn along the centre of Pinck- ney and Ferry streets on the Southeast and a line drawn along the centre of Main street on the Northeast shall be known as Ward Four .

Sec . 3. That the said city shall be governed by a Mayor Mayor and and eight Aldermen , who shall be citizens of the United Aldermen . States , qualified electors of said city , who shall have been
domiciled in the State one year and in the city sixty days next before their election , and shall continue in office for two years from the day of their election , and until their suc- cessors are elected and qualified ; that the Mayor and one Election and Alderman for each ward shall be elected during one year , and one Alderman for each ward the next year , and so on in each alternate year ; that the present Intendant and four Wardens of the town of Abbeville shall be the Mayor and four of the Aldermen of the city of Abbeville until the regu- lar city election , which shall be held on the second Tuesday in April , 1896 , and that one Alderman from each ward shall be elected on the second Tuesday in April , 1895 , as herein- after provided , and that thereafter the regular city election shall be held on the second Tuesday in April of each year ; that the Mayor and Aldermen shall take the oath of office prescribed by the Constitution of this State before entering on the discharge of their official duties , and a majority of Quorum . the Council shall constitute a quorum to transact business ; that the Mayor shall be paid for his services such compensa- Mayor's salary . tion as the City Council by ordinance fix , which shall not be diminished during his term of office ; that in case the Mayor be temporarily absent or unable to attend to the duties of his office , from sickness or other cause , the Aldermen shall have power to elect any one of their number to serve as Mayor pro tempore ; that the City Council shall hold stated Mayor pro tem . meetings at least once in each month , and such other meet- ings as it may desire ; that the Mayor shall nominate at the commencement of his term , subject to the approval of the City Council by vote , such committees to transact the public business as the Council may by ordinance determine . That the City Council shall elect a Clerk and Treasurer , a Superin- tendent of Streets , such policemen as may be necessary , and such other officers as may be necessary to transact the busi- ness of the city ; and it may by ordinance prescribe the duties of said officers and may fix the salaries of the same and require bonds of them for the faithful performance of their duty ; that the policemen shall take the oath prescribed by law for Constables , and shall have all the powers and be charged with all the liabilities now or hereafter incident to the office of Constable ; and they may arrest and commit to the guard house of the city for speedy trial any person who , within the corporate limits , may be engaged in a breach of the peace , riotous or disorderly conduct , open obscenity , public drunkenness , or any conduct grossly indecent or dan- gerous to the citizens of said city . All of said officers shall be liable to removal at the pleasure of the Council . That the Clerk of Council shall annually , on the first day of April , make out and publish on the court house door in said city , and file in the office of Council , an itemized statement of the receipts and disbursements of the city during the preceding year ; and when a new Council has been elected and sworn in , then the outgoing Council shall forthwith turn over to it all the records , property and funds belonging to the said city , and a failure to do so without reasonable excuse for twenty - four hours after a demand , in writing , so to do shall subject the members of the outgoing Council to a fine of five hundred dollars , to be recovered by the City Council for the use of said city in any Court of competent jurisdiction .

Sec . 4. That the election for Mayor and Aldermen herein- before provided for shall be held , at such place as may be designated by the City Council , from nine o'clock A. M. until four o'clock P. M. , and that at least ten days ' notice thereof be given by publication in a newspaper at Abbeville ; that such election shall be conducted by three Managers to be appointed by the City Council , one of whom shall be Chair- man and another clerk , and all of whom shall , before enter- ing on their duties , take an oath to fairly and impartially conduct the election ; that the said Managers , or any of them , shall administer to every person offering to vote at Oath for voter . the election an oath that he is duly qualified to vote at such election according to the Constitution and laws of this State , and has not voted before at this election ; that said Managers shall keep a correct list of the names of the per- sons voting and of those offering to vote at such election , shall count the ballots , cast up the result and proclaim the election and file the lists and results with the Clerk of Coun- cil , who shall forthwith notify in writing the persons who have received a plurality of the ballots cast ; that in the event no candidate should receive a plurality of the votes cast , or in the event of a vacancy in office caused by death , resignation or otherwise , another election shall be ordered in like manner as the first , but one registration in any one year shall be sufficient ; that in said elections all male citi- zens over the age of twenty - one years who have been domi- ciled in the State one year and in the city sixty days next before the election , and who have been registered as herein- after provided , and who are not disqualified by law , shall be entitled to vote .

Sec . 5. That the Clerk of Council shall annually , on the second Tuesday in March and the Wednesday and Thursday succeeding , between the hours of nine o'clock A. M. and three o'clock P. M. , at the office of said Clerk , open a list for Registration . the registration of qualified voters of said city , on which list shall be shown in writing the name , age , occupation and ward of residence of the voter , and any person who shall attain the age of twenty - one years after the said time of registration and before the next succeeding day of election , and is not otherwise disqualified , shall be allowed to regis- ter at such registration . Notice of said registration shall be given for two weeks previous thereto by publication in one or more newspapers published in said city of Abbeville and by posting on the court house door . The certificate of registration shall be signed by said Clerk and issued to each person registering in the following form :

This is to certify that ... of Ward ...... of the city of Abbeville ... years of age , and entitled to vote in the municipal election of said city . Clerk of Council .

After each municipal election only such persons shall be required to register as shall become entitled to vote at each Subsequent approaching election . At each subsequent registration the said Clerk shall revise the registration lists and erase there- from the names of all registered voters who have died or become disqualified to vote since the previous election . The said registration lists shall at all times be open to the in- spection of the qualified voters of the city , shall be carefully preserved by the Clerk of Council , and on annual or any special elections shall be placed in the possession of the Managers appointed to conduct the election , and at the close of such election shall be returned by said Managers to said Clerk .

Sec . 6. That the Mayor and Aldermen collectively and severally are hereby vested with the jurisdiction and powers within the city limits which Trial Justices now have or may hereafter have , except in civil actions ; that they shall be designated as the City Council of Abbeville ; may have a common seal ; may sue and be sued ; may purchase or re- ceive by gift or devise , and hold , personal and real property , not to exceed in value in the aggregate at any one time $ 100,000.00 , and may sell , alien or lease the same ; may bor- row money and execute evidences of debt , but such debts shall not exceed $ 10,000 at any one time ; may make such ordinances respecting sidewalks , streets , drainage , natural water courses , powder house or houses for storing explo- sives , the interment of human bodies , the running of rail- road cars or engines , butchers , livery stables , public drays or vehicles , live stock , places of amusement , public houses , saloons , auctioneers , itinerant tradesmen or peddlers , shows , circuses or exhibitions , and such other matters pertaining to the concerns of said corporation as shall be proper , neces- sary or advisable for the preservation or safety of the peace , order , comfort , health , convenience and welfare of the citi- Fines and zens of said city ; may fix and impose fines and penalties for the violation of law or its ordinances , but no fine or penalty shall exceed one hundred dollars or imprisonment in the guard house for a longer period than thirty days , or by sentence to work on the streets for thirty days , and the judgment may be in the alternative ; and may abate and re- move all nuisances in the said city ..

Sec . 7. That the said City Council shall annually , during the month of August , appoint three citizens of the said city to assess in that month the value of all the taxable prop- erty therein , and the said appraisers shall ascertain from Assessments . the taxpayers in person the true value of all their real and personal and mixed estates situated in said city , and enter the same in a book in separate columns , and it shall be signed by the appraisers and returned to the Clerk of Coun- cil forthwith ; but the taxpayers shall have thirty days from the return of said assessment in which to complain thereof to the City Council , upon the entering of which the Council may lessen any assessment upon good cause shown . That upon the values so ascertained the City Council shall , during the month of October , levy a tax for corporate pur- poses not to exceed in any year five mills on the dollar , pay- able in advance to the Clerk and Treasurer of the Council during the months of November and December in each year : Provided , That the provisions of this Section shall not in- terfere with the levy and collection of the taxes for the town of Abbeville for the present year during the months of February and March next , but shall go into effect imme- diately thereafter ; and all property upon which such taxes shall be levied shall be subject to a first lien for the payment thereof , except for debts due to the State ; and upon failure of any person to pay such tax , the party in fault shall be 
subject to the penalties and remedies provided , or which may hereafter be provided , by law for failure to pay State and County taxes , except that the execution for the collec- tion thereof shall be signed and sealed by the Clerk and Treasurer of the Council and directed to a police officer of the said city .

Sec . 8. That the said City Council may grant or refuse licenses to keepers of livery stables , drivers of public drays , hacks and vehicles kept for hire , butchers , auctioneers , ped- dlers , itinerant tradesmen , keepers of billiard tables , ten- pin alleys , or any other kind of game , exhibitions of skill or chance within said corporation , and the said City Council may impose a license fee on any of the said occupants , and also on any person who keeps a store , shop , office or other place of business and carries on his trade , profession or business in said city but resides and holds his property beyond the limits of said city , thus escaping his or her just share of the burdens of the city government ; and said City Council may enforce the collection of said license fees , which shall be turned into the city treasury 

Sec . 9. That persons charged with the violation of law or the ordinances of said city shall undergo trial before the Trials . Mayor or before the Council , as the defendant may elect , and with or without the intervention of a jury ; that the Mayor or Council may require the attendance of witnesses and require them to give testimony upon the trial of any cause then pending , and shall be governed by the same rules of procedure and evidence as are now or may hereafter be prescribed for the government of the Courts of Trial Jus- tices ; and the party charged with an offense shall be cited to trial by the service upon him of a summons under the Summons . hand of the Mayor , unless the offense is committed in full view of an officer , wherein shall be specified the offense charged and the time and place of trial and wherein the City Council shall be plaintiff ; that the said Council shall keep a book wherein shall be entered the names of parties Docket . charged with the violation of law or ordinances , the date of trial and the judgment in such case ; that fines so im- posed may be collected by an execution issued under the hand and seal of the Clerk and Treasurer , tested by the corporate seal and directed to a policeman of the corpora-
tion , who shall seize such property of the defendant as shall be subject to levy and sale and sell in a public place the same to satisfy the judgment , after two weeks ' advertise- ment on the court house door .

Sec . 10. That the said City Council is hereby invested Jurisdiction with ample jurisdiction over the streets , alleys and side- walks within the corporate limits ; to extend or close , widen or narrow , lay out , grade , curb , pave and otherwise improve streets , alleys and sidewalks ; to build bridges in and cul- verts under said streets ; to prevent or remove any structure or obstruction or encroachment over or in or under said streets , alleys or sidewalks , and may permit the planting of shade trees along said streets ; to prevent any company or persons from occupying with its or their works , or any ap- purtenances thereof , the streets , alleys or sidewalks of the city without the consent of Council ; to prevent the cumber- ing of streets , sidewalks , alleys , lanes or bridges in the city in any manner whatever ; and for the purpose of opening new streets or of widening or changing existing streets , the Condemnation . City Council may condemn lands or buildings , or parts thereof , but just compensation therefor shall first be made to the owner , and if the City Council and such owner fail to agree upon the amount of such compensation the same may be fixed as follows , to wit : The City Council shall nominate two citizens of the corporation , the owner of the property shall nominate two other citizens of the corporation , and these four shall nominate a fifth other citizen of the corpo- ration , and these five citizens shall constitute a commission to examine the locus in quo , to take testimony and assess the compensation , after having first been sworn to decide justly and impartially in the premises ; and they shall file their decision with the Clerk of the Circuit Court for the County of Abbeville within ten days from the time of their appointment , and it shall be final unless either party ap- peals therefrom to the Court of Common Pleas for said County by serving on the other party within five days after the filing of such decision a notice of appeal ; and in that case the issue of compensation shall be submitted to a jury at the term of the Circuit Court next thereafter ensuing . In the event the property owner refuses to nominate two commissioners or fails to do so within five days after he is notified to do so , then they shall be nominated by the Clerk of the Circuit Court for the County of Abbeville , and the fifth commissioner shall be chosen as before . The said com- missioners shall be entitled to receive one dollar each for their services , to be paid by the City Council , but the costs of appeal shall be paid by the losing party . That for the purpose of keeping the streets , alleys , sidewalks , bridges , drains and culverts in repair , or for laying out and con- structing new streets , all the male citizens of said corpora- tion between the ages of sixteen and fifty - five years shall render to the City Council personal service therein for at least five days in each year , at such time as they may be called on by the corporate authorities ; but such services may be commuted by the payment of two and 50-100 dollars to compound tax . the Treasurer of the city at the time of the annual payment of taxes , herein before provided for , to be expended for like purposes ; and in the event any person liable to perform such service shall refuse or fail to render the same , after notice of the time and place to serve , the said City Council or the Mayor shall have the power to try such person for such offense , and if found guilty to sentence him to as much as thirty days ' imprisonment or thirty days ' labor on the streets or to pay a fine of as much as thirty dollars , to be collected as other fines are collected . Members of the City Council shall be exempt from such duty , and all citizens of Privileges of said corporation shall be exempt from road duty without the corporation . That whenever any new street is to be laid out or opened , a street graded or paved , a culvert built or any other public improvement constructed , the City Council shall determine what proportion , if any , of the cost Cost of streets . thereof shall be paid out of the city treasury and what pro- portion by the owners of real estate to be benefited thereby ; but no such public improvement shall be made , to be de- frayed in whole or in part by local assessment , until it has been requested to be undertaken by at least a majority of the owners of the property to be assessed for such improve- ment ; and such assessments shall be collected in the same manner as is the cost of the construction of sidewalks . That the said City Council may require all persons owning and occupying a lot or lots on any street or alley in the said city to construct and keep in good repair sidewalks abutting such lot or lots , and the Council may designate the width of such sidewalks and the manner of their construction ; and in the event the owner shall refuse or neglect to comply with such requirement or regulation , the City Council may repair or construct the said sidewalks and recover from the owner the cost thereof in a Court of competent jurisdiction ; but the contract for such repairs or construction must first have been let out to the lowest bidder after notice by one publi- cation in a newspaper in said city .

Sec . 11. That the said City Council may establish and Fire depart- maintain a fire department for the extinguishment of fires , and to that end may purchase engines and pumps and hose , and construct tanks and reservoirs , and dig wells and lay pipes ; that it may secure the services of firemen , either by exemption from public municipal duties , or by payment of money , and to this end it may pass all proper ordinances and make appropriations from the city treasury for the establishment and support of such department . And the said City Council shall have full power to prevent the erec- Wooden build- tion of any wooden or frame building , or any wooden roof , in any section of said city which they may by ordinance de- fine ; and they are empowered to pass ordinance to carry into effect the provisions of this Section , and may abate such buildings as a nuisance .

Sec . 12. That the said City Council may construct , have Water works . constructed or purchase public works for the supply of pure water to the citizens of said corporation , may operate the same , and may sell the water to consumers ; may construct , have constructed or purchase public works for the genera- Gas or electric tion of gas or electricity for purposes of light , may operate the same , and sell light to consumers ; and to these ends it may pass all ordinances necessary or proper for the regula- No bonds , un- tion and control of such works : Provided , That no bonded obligation shall be incurred by said city until that question has been submitted to a popular election therein , and shall have been approved by a majority of the voters then voting . That the said City Council shall have the power to grant a franchise or franchises for the erection or construction of such light and water works to private parties or corporation upon such terms and restrictions , to be incorporated in such grant , as may be necessary and proper to secure and protect the interests of said city and its citizens . But no such grant shall be made for a longer period than thirty years .

Sec . 13. That this Act shall take effect from and after its passage ; that all other Acts conferring powers on the town Consistent Acts of Abbeville , and not herein referred to nor inconsistent with this Act , are continued of full force ; that the ordi- Also ordinances . nances of the town of Abbeville are hereby continued , to be of full force and effect for the government of the city of Abbeville until repealed or modified by other ordinances by the City Council ; all the obligations and contracts of the town of Abbeville and to the town of Abbeville are hereby continued as the valid and subsisting obligations and con- tracts of and to the city of Abbeville ; and all the property of the town of Abbeville is hereby vested in the city of Ab- beville .

Sec . 14. That this Act is a public Act , and shall continue of force for thirty years next hereafter ; and all Acts or pealing clause . parts of Acts inconsistent with this Act are hereby re- pealed .
