Year:1913       ACT NO.:121
AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR CREATING A HIGHWAY COMMISSION FOR ABBEVILLE COUNTY, DEFINE ITS POWERS AND DUTIES, AND TO PROVIDE FOR FUNDS TO CARRY OUT THE OBJECT OF SAID COMMISSION.

Section 1. Highway Commission for Abbeville County.—Le it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That there is hereby created in Abbeville county a commission, con- sisting of five men, who shall be known as the Highway Commission of Abbeville County, and who shall have such powers and duties as are given them under this Act, or that may hereafter be conferred upon them by law. 

§ 2. Appointment.—The said Commissionefs shall be appointed by the Governor upon the recommendation of the Abbeville Delegation in the General Assembly. 

§ 3. Terms of Office.—That the terms of said Highway Com- missioners shall be for two years each, unless removed by the Gov- ernor upon the recommendation of Abbeville Delegation in the Gen- eral Assembly. 

§ 4. Jurisdiction That said Highway Commission shall have full jurisdiction over the roads and highways of Abbeville county, as far as in their judgment are necessary or proper for them to assume, for the purpose of building, laying out, widening and main- taining the roads of Abbeville county; and they are hereby empow- ered to take charge of such roads as in their judgment may be neces- sary or advisable by giving the Board of County Commissioners five days’ notice of their intention, and it shall be the duty of the Super- visor to turn over such roads as they may demand to the jurisdiction of said Highway Commission. 

§ 5. Oath and Bond.—That said Highway Commission, when appointed according to the terms of this Act, shall take the oath of office provided by the Constitution of this State, and shall each give bond in the sum of five thousand dollars for the faithful perform- ance of his duties as such Commissioner ; said bond to be approved by the Clerk of the Circuit Court, both as to its form and sufficiency. 

§ 6. Authorized to Issue Bonds.—That said Highway Commis- sion is hereby authorized to issue bonds of the county of Abbeville to the amount of one hundred and eighty thousand ($180,000) dol- lars, for the purpose of raising money to carry out the objects of this Act; said bonds to be in the denomination of five hundred dollars each, to be payable in twenty years, and to bear a rate of interest not exceeding five per cent. per annum, and to be styled and called High- way Bonds of Abbeville County. Said Commission shall advertise said bonds for sale by publishing notices thereof in such newspapers as they may deem best calculated to secure bidders, and shall sell said bonds to the highest bidders, for cash, in such quantities as they may be able to get the best price for; said bonds when issued shall be exempt from State and county taxes, and the coupons shall be receivable for county taxes. 

§ 7. Proceeds of Sale of Bonds.—That, as soon as said bonds are sold, the proceeds of said sale shall be deposited in three or more of the banks in Abbeville county, as the Commission may determine, upon such terms and conditions as the Commission and the banks may agree upon, and shall only be drawn out upon checks signed by said Commission, or a majority of its members, for the purposes con- templated in this Act: Provided, That should said Commission desire to lend any of said funds on short time loans, before it is needed to use in the building of roads, it shall have the right to do so, taking proper security therefor. All interest on such loans to be added to the sinking fund, for the ultimate retirement of said bonds. 

§ 8. Proceeds—How Used.—That out of the proceeds of said bonds the said Commission shall use so much as may be necessary in building a system of good roads in Abbeville county, of a perma- nent and lasting character, and maintain the same in good condition. 

§ 9. Civil Engineer.—That in order to carry out the objects of this Act the said Highway Commission shall employ a competent civil engineer, whose duty it shall be to make a survey of the roads of the county, which the said Commission desires to build or improve, and who shall superintend the building of such roads as he may be ordered to build by said Commission, and who shall be at all times subject to the orders of said Commision. He shall be paid such sal- ary as may be determined by said Commission, not exceeding the sum of eighteen hundred ($1,800) dollars per year. That said engineer shall have the right to enter upon any lands in the county for the purpose of making surveys for roads, provided that he shall do no injury to the owner of the land, in the way of cutting timber or destroying crops, fences, or other property of the landowner. 

§ 10. Annual Tax Levy for Interest and Sinking Fund.—That for the purpose of paying interest on said bonds, and providing a sinking fund for their retirements, there is hereby levied upon all the taxable property of Abbeville county a tax of two and one-half mills upon the dollar, which shall be due and payable at the same time and upon the same terms as other county taxes, and shall be listed by the Auditor and collected by the Treasurer of the county, as is provided by law for the other taxes of the county. 

§ 11. Highway Commission Fund.—That out of the amount of taxes so collected the said Treasurer shall pay to the bondholders the interest on said bonds, as it shall become due, and the remainder of said taxes shall be set apart as the Highway Commission fund, and shall be drawn out only upon the warrants of said Highway Commission, signed by said Commission, or a majority thereof. That it shall be the duty of said Highway Commission to invest all moneys arising out of the taxes hereby levied, except that paid for interest on the bonds, and the salaries of the engineer and Commis- sion, in some safe security, at as good rate of interest as possible: Provided, That the rate of interest shall not be less than seven per cent., for the purpose of a sinking fund to retire said bonds at maturity, and said sinking fund shall never be used for any purpose except that herein set forth, and shall be held as a trust fund, for the benefit of the holders of said highway bonds. In lending said money preference shall be given to real estate security in Abbeville county, wherever the same can be had on as good terms as other securities. 

§ 12. Maintain Office.—That said Highway Commission shall maintain an office at the courthouse, which shall be kept open at all times for the transaction of business pertaining to said Commission, and shall be in charge of one of said Commissioners, who shall be elected clerk by said Commission at its first meeting, and who shall hold his office for such time as may be determined by said Commis- sion. That said Commissioners shall each be paid a salary of two hundred dollars per year, except the secretary, who shall receive a salary of six hundred dollars per year; said salaries to be paid quar- terly, upon the warrants of the Commission, out of the funds of said Commission. Said Commission shall meet at least once a month, and at such other times as they may call extra meetings, and shall be presided over by one of their number, to be elected by said Commis- sion, and shall be designated as the chairman thereof. That all roads of the county, taken in charge by said Commission, shall be worked by contract, let to the lowest responsible bidder, who shall be required to give bond to the Commission for the faithful discharge of his contract and who shall work under the direction and control of the Road Engineer. 

§ 13. May Condemn Lands.—That in case it becomes necessary to condemn any land for the purpose of building, repairing, chang- ing, or in any manner working the roads and highways of this county, said Commission is hereby granted the right to condemn lands for said purpose, or for any of them, which land shall be condemned in the following manner, that is to say, the said Commis- sioners shall select six freeholders of the county, the landowner, whose lands it is desired to condemn, shall select six, and said twelve shall proceed to condemn the land required, and determine its value, and the amount so agreed upon shall be paid to the landowner within ten days after said condemnation proceedings are reported to the Commission out of the funds under the control of the Commission for that purpose. Should said twelve freeholders be equally divided in opinion, and thus fail to agree, they shall have the right to select another freeholder, and a majority of the said jury shall determine the compensation to be paid. If either party is dissatisfied with the amount awarded by the jury for the land required, then the Commission, or the landholder, shall have the right to appeal to the Court of Common Pleas, and the case shall be tried before a jury, upon issues to be submitted to them by the Court, and whose decision on all questions shall be final, unless set aside by the presiding Judge: Provided, however, That the appeal shall not stay the acquiring of the land by the Highway Commission, but the amount agreed on for the land to be deposited with the Clerk of the Court to await the ‘result of the appeal. 

§ 14, Election to Be Held.—That the question of whether this Act shall become law or not shall be submitted to an election to be held by the voters of Abbeville county, on the second Tues- day in August, 1913: Provided, A petition, signed by one-third of the qualified electors of Abbeville county, be filed with the Supervisor of said county on or before the fifteenth day of June. 1913, asking for said election; which said election shall be held at the regular voting precincts of Abbeville county, under the same rules and regulations as the regular elections for State and county officers are held, the managers of said election to be appointed by the Board of County Commissioners of Abbeville county not less than two weeks nor more than four weeks before said election, and the returns from said election, consisting of the poll lists, ballots and returns of the managers, shall be filed with the Board of County Commissioners within three davs after said election; which board shall assemble and declare the result of said election in not less than one week from the date thereof. At such election the ballots shall be printed and furnished by the Board of County Commissioners to the managers of election. and there shall be printed on said ballots the following words. to wit: “In favor of bonds for roads,” “Opposed to bonds for roads,” and an equal number of said ballots shall be furnished of both kinds. If a majority of the legal and qualified voters of Abbeville county shall vote in favor of bonds for roads, then the above Act shall be and hecome the law. and shall go into effect on the first day of September, 1913, and the elections for said Commissioners shall be held, as provided by this Act, not later than September 15, 1913. Should a majority of the legal and qualified voters of Abbeville county vote against bonds for roads, then this Act shall be and void and of no force and effect whatever. 


Year:1913       ACT NO.:127
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE SCHOOL TRUSTEES IN CERTAIN DISTRICTS TO PURCHASE AND MAINTAIN LIBRARIES.

Section 1. Trustees in Certain School Districts Authorized to Maintain Libraries—Proviso.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, In school districts in which are situated towns or cities of more than three thousand inhabitants the trustees are hereby authorized to appropriate out of the annual levy for the support of such schools such sum as may seem to them wise, not exceeding three per cent. of the amount annually raised, for the purchase and maintenance of libraries: Provided, That the provisions of this Act shall apply only to Spartanburg county. 


Year:1913       ACT NO.:144
AN ACT TO REQUIRE ALL SUPPLIES FOR CERTAIN STATE INSTITUTIONS TO BE PURCHASED IN OPEN MARKET AFTER DUE ADVERTISEMENT.

Section 1. Purchase of Supplies for State Hospital for Insane and Penitentiary.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That on and after approval of this Act, all regular supplies for the State Hospital for the Insane, the State Penitentiary and the Confederate Home shall be purchased in the open market in the following manner, to wit: The officers now authorized to purchase said supplies shall duly advertise, in one or more daily papers, once a week for three consecutive weeks, for bids to furnish said supplies for a period of three months. 

§ 2. Bids—That all bids shall be opened publicly by said officer, who shall accept the best and lowest bid made for the furnishing of said supplies 

§ 3. Successful Bidder to Enter Into Contract.—The successful bidder shall enter into an agreement or contract to furnish said supplies at such times during said three months as he may be directed by the said officers, and shall give a good and sufficient bond in the sum ‘of double the amount of said bid, conditioned for the faithful performance of said contract The said bond shall be in favor of the State, and shall be collected as other bonds of such nature are now collected § 4. Inconsistent Acts Repealed.—That all Acts or parts of Acts inconsistent with this Act are hereby repealed § 5. Immediately Effective—This Act shall go into effect immediately on approval by the Governor.

§ 40. Governor , Treasurer and Comptroller General Author- ized to Borrow Funds . That in anticipation of the taxes herein- before levied , the Governor and the State Treasurer and the Comptroller General be , and they are hereby , empowered to bor- row on credit of the State so much money from time to time as may be needed to meet promptly , at maturity , the interest which will mature on the first day of July and on the first day of January of each year , on the valid debt of the State , and to pay the current expenses of the State government for the present fiscal year , and for pensions : Provided , The sum so borrowed shall not exceed the sum of six hundred thousand ( $ 600,000 ) dollars .

§ 41. Expenditures Not to Exceed Appropriations . It shall not be lawful for any expenditure authorized under the various sections of this Act to exceed the amount specifically appropriated therefor .

§ 42. Immediately Effective . - This Act shall take effect imme- diately upon its approval by the Governor .

§ 43. One Mill School Tax Fund - Provision to Borrow Funds . -That in anticipation of a one ( 1 ) mill levy and the taxes derived therefrom as provided by Act of the General Assembly of South Carolina passed in 1913 , entitled " An Act to levy and collect one ( 1 ) mill State tax for the free public school and to pro- vide for the distribution of the same , the Governor , State Treas- urer and the Comptroller General be , and they are hereby , empow- ered to borrow on the credit of the State so much money as from time to time as may be needed to pay for the objects and purposes set forth in the Act above referred to : Provided , The sum so borrowed shall not exceed one hundred and fifty thousand ( $ 150,000 ) dollars .

§ 44. Appropriations - How Paid . — That the appropriation made herein for the officers and employees shall be paid as sálaries to the persons holding the positions designated .


Year:1913       ACT NO.:151
AN ACT TO AMEND AN ACT ENTITLED ""AN ACT TO ESTABLISH THE UNION SCHOOL DISTRICT, TO AUTHORIZE THE ESTABLISHMENT OF FREE GRADED SCHOOLS THEREIN, AND TO PROVIDE MEANS FOR THE EFFICIENT MANAGEMENT OF THE SAME.""

Section 1. Union School District - Act Amended . - Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina , That Section 3 of said Act be amended by striking out the word " three " between the words " exceeding " and " mills " on line 4 , and insert- ing in lieu thereof the word " five . " Amend further by striking out the word " three " on line 18 , and inserting in lieu thereof the word " five ; " so that , when amended , said section shall read as follows :

Section 3. That said trustees are hereby authorized and empow- ered , on or before the first day of June in each year , to levy on all real and personal property returned for taxation in said school district a local tax not exceeding five mills on the dollar in any one year , to supplement the general tax for the support of schools , by the persons and in the mode following , to wit : The Board of Trustees , on or before the fifteenth day of May in each year , shall call a meeting of all the legal voters living in the said school dis- trict and returning real or personal property therein : Provided , That public notice of said meeting , specifying the time , place and object , shall be given at least ten days before said meeting by posting the same in three conspicuous places in said school dis- trict and publishing the same at least twice in a newspaper , if any published , in said school district . The persons answering the above description when thus assembled shall appoint a chairman , and also a secretary , adjourn from time to time , and decide what additional tax , if any , shall be levied , not to exceed five mills on the dollar . No tax thus levied shall be repealed at a subsequent meeting within the same fiscal year . The chairman shall one week thereafter notify the County Auditor of Union county of the amount of tax levied , and the County Auditor shall at once assess such tax on all real and personal property returned in said school district , and the County Treasurer of said county shall collect said tax with the other taxes for the same year , and the said tax shall be collected and enforced in the same manner pro- vided for State and county taxes .


Year:1913       ACT NO.:152
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE TOWN OF LAMAR, IN DARLINGTON COUNTY, UPON THE PETITION OF A MAJORITY OF ITS FREEHOLDERS AND THE VOTE OF A MAJORITY OF ITS ELECTORS, QUALIFIED, TO VOTE AT AN ELECTION THEREON, TO ISSUE NOT MORE THAN SEVEN THOUSAND DOLLARS IN
BONDS IN AID OF THE SOUTH CAROLINA WESTERN RAILWAY, AND TO LEVY AND COLLECT TAXES TO PAY THE INTEREST ON THE SAID BONDS AND THE PRINCIPAL THEREOF.

Whereas, The South Carolina Western Railway is now build- ing and constructing a line of railroad which is to be operated from the town of Lydia, through the town of Lamar to the town of Timmonsville in Florence county, in the State of South Carolina; and Whereas, The opening up of this new line of transportation is expected to be of great benefit and advantage to the commercial welfare of the town of Lamar and vicinity, and the citizens of the same town have agreed to raise certain funds to secure a ight of way and a depot site through the town of Lamar for the said railroad in consideration of the benefit and advantage to accrue to them from the construction and operation of said railroad 

Section 1. Bond Election for Town of Lamar.—De it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That upon a petition of a majority of the freeholders of the town of Lamar, Darlington county, as shown by its tax books, to hold a special election in said town for the purpose of submitting to the qualified electors residing in said town of Lamar, at an election upon the question of issuing bonds to an amount not to exceed seven thousand dollars for the purpose of aiding in the building and construction of the South Carolina Western Railway, that the Town Council of said town is authorized and empowered to order an election upon said bond issue, at which election all persons qualified to vote in said election shall be allowed to vote and the said Town Council shall give ‘two weeks’ notice in some newspaper published in the county, which notice shall state the time, place and purpose of said election 

§ 2. Town Council to Appoint Managers, etc.—The said Town Council of the town of Lamar shall appoint the managers, pre scribe the form of ballot to be used, receive the returns and declare the result of said election. 

§ 3. Bond Issue.—That in case a majority of votes cast in said election be in favor of said bond issue, the bonds shall be issued and they shall bear interest at a rate not to exceed six per cent payable annually, and they shall be of the par value of one hun- dred dollars each; they shall be signed by the Intendant or Mayor of the town, and shall be countersigned by the Clerk of the Town Council, and they shall mature twenty years after date, and the coupons thereof shall be receivable for town taxes, and any or all of said bonds may be redeemable by the said town at any time after the elapse of five years from their date at the option of the Town Council of the town of Lamar 

§ 4. Sale of Bonds.—That the said bonds, or any part thereof, may be sold by the Town Council, either at public or private sale. 

§ 5. Tax Levy to Pay Interest on Bonds.—That it shall be the duty of the said Town Council to levy and collect annually a tax upon all property in said town subject to taxation, both real and personal, sufficient to pay the interest on said bonds as it may become due, this tax to be in addition to that levied and collected for ordinary purposes. 

§ 6. Sinking Fund—Proviso.—In addition to the tax herein- before provided to meet the annual interest of said bonds, and in addition to the taxes for ordinary purposes, the Town Council of the town of Lamar, shall levy and collect annually a tax on all property in said town subject to taxation, both real and personal, to be not, less than ten per cent. of the face value of said bonds, which said sum shall be denominated a sinking fund, and which shall be applied to the extinguishment of said bonds whenever they shall be retired: Provided,.That the sums collected for said sinking fund shall be invested by the Town Council of the town of Lamar, in safe interest- bearing securing, applied on the liquidation and payment of said bonds before their maturity. 

§ 7. Immediately Effective.—This Act shall take effect immedi- ately upon its approval by the Governor, and all Acts or parts of Acts inconsistent with this Act are hereby repealed. 


Year:1913       ACT NO.:153
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE TRUSTEES OF ROCK HILL SCHOOL DISTRICT, ROCK HILL, S. C., TO ISSUE BONDS FOR SCHOOL PURPOSES.

Section 1. Rock Hill School District Authorized to Issue Bonds—Provisos.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That the Trustees of Rock Hill School District, Rock Hill, county of York, State aforesaid, are hereby authorized and empowered to issue and sell coupon bonds of said school district in an amount not exceeding seventy-five thousand ($75,000) dollars, in such sum or sums as they may deem necessary, for the purpose of paying off past indebtedness, purchasing a lot or lots, building one or more buildings, or altering or repairing, or add- ing to existing buildings, and equipping same, in said district as said trustees may deem advisable: Provided, That the School Trustees 

be allowed and permitted to use not more than nine thousand dollars, if that much be necessary, of the said sum of seventy-five thousand dollars to refund to the City Council of Rock Hill, S. C., the amount of principal, with interest, that it has expended in the purchase of the lot and erecting the buildings on what is known as the Graded School lot, situated in the incorporated limits of the city of Rock Hill, S. C.: And provided, further, That the question of issuing the bonds authorized in this section shall be first submitted to the qualified voters of said school district at an election to be held to determine whether said bonds shall be issued or not, as hereinafter provided. § 2. Election to Be Held.—That for the purpose of determining the issue of bonds as authorized in Section one (1) of this Act, the said trustees shall order an election to be held in said school district, on the question of whether said bonds shall be issued, in which elec- tion only the qualified voters residing in said district shall be allowed to vote; and the said trustees shall publish notice once a week for two weeks in The Evening Herald and in The Record, newspapers published in Rock Hill; shall designate the time and place or places of voting, and appoint the managers of such election, receive the return of the managers, and declare the result. 

§ 3. Ballots.——The said trustees shall have printed for the use of the voters in said election two (2) sets of ballots, a sufficient num- ber of each of which shall be placed at each voting place; on one set of ballots shall be printed the words, “For the Issuing of Bonds,” and on the other set shall be printed the. words, “Against the Issuing of Bonds.” If the majority of votes cast at said election shall be for the issuing of bonds, the said trustees may issue said bonds or such an amount thereof not exceeding seventy-five thousand ($75,000) dollars, as they may deem advisable for the purpose set forth in Section one (1) of this Act payable to bearer, at such place or places as the said trustees may designate, to run for not more than twenty years from the date of issue, bearing interest at the rate not exceed- ing five (5) per centum per annum, payable annually or semiannu- ally. Any bonds not issued shall be cancelled. 

§ 4. Seal Authorized—Proviso.—That the said Board of Trus- tees are hereby authorized to adopt and make a seal for their official use in the execution of said bonds and like important papers; that said bonds shall be signed by the Chairman and countersigned by the Secretary and Treasurer of the Board of Trustees of said district, and the official seal of said board attached thereto: Provided, That the signatures of said officers may be lithographed, or printed or engraved on the coupons attached to said bonds, and such signatures shall be a sufficient signing thereof. 

§ 5. Annual Tax Levy to Pay Interest—Proviso.—That it shall be the duty of the county officers of York county charged with the assessment and collection of taxes, by the direction of said trustees of said school district, to levy such a tax annually upon all property, real and personal, within said district and collect the same as taxes for the State, county and school purposes are now levied and collected, as will raise a sufficient sum to pay the interest on all bonds issued under and in pursuance of this Act, and also a sum sufficient to pro- vide a sinking fund for the payment of such bonds when due: Pro- vided, That Board of Trustees are hereby authorized to deposit said sinking fund'in such bank or banks as are designated to receive State and county funds, or may otherwise safely invest said fund, if they deem it wise to do so. § 6. Bonds Exempt from Taxation.—Said bonds shall be exempt from State, county and municipal taxation. 

§ 7. Immediately Effective——That this Act shall take effect immediately upon its approval by the Governor, and all Acts and parts of Acts inconsistent herewith are hereby repealed.  


Year:1913       ACT NO.:155
AN ACT RELATING TO SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 30, IN NEWBERRY COUNTY.
Section 1. Trustees of School District No. 30 , Newberry County , May Issue Coupon Bonds . - Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina , That for the purpose of paying off and retiring the bonds of School District No. 30 , in New- berry county , heretofore issued by said school district , the trustees of said school district are hereby authorized and required to issue coupon bonds to the amount of $ 2,000 , dated April 1st , 1913 ; that is to say , twenty bonds of the face value of $ 100 each , bearing inter- est at six per cent . per annum , payable annually , one of said bonds to be paid each year , beginning April 1st , 1914 : Provided , That a majority of the qualified electors of said school district voting shall be in favor of such issue at an election hereafter to be held .

§ 2. Election Notice . That the trustees of said school district are hereby required to give two weeks ' previous notice , in one or more of the newspapers published in the county of Newberry , of the time and place of such election , appoint the managers , prescribe the form of ballot , receive the returns and declare the result of such election .

§ 3. Bonds Signed - How . - That said bonds shall be signed by the chairman of the trustees and countersigned by the secretary . The coupons attached to said bonds shall be receivable in payment of any taxes in said school district . The said bonds shall be exempt from taxation for State , county and municipal purposes .

§ 4. Annual Tax Levy to Pay Bonds and Interest . That for the purpose of paying said bonds and the interest thereon , the Audi- tor of Newberry county , or such other officer as may be charged with the assessment of taxes , shall annually levy a tax of four and one- half mills on all the taxable property in said school district , and the amount so levied shall be collected by the County Treasurer of New- berry county as State and county taxes are collected , to be held and applied by him as follows , viz .: To the payment of said bonds and interest thereon , and any surplus remaining after the payment of the bonds and interest on all unpaid bonds each year , to be turned into the general funds of the said school district and applied to the cur- rent expenses of maintaining schools in said school district .

§ 5. Disposition of Bonds and Proceeds . - That the trustees of said school district shall apply said bonds , or the proceeds of the sale

OF SOUTH CAROLINA . 289

thereof , together with any funds in the hands of the County Treas- urer derived under the levy for the payment of the existing bonded indebtedness of said school district , to the payment and retirement of the outstanding bonds of said school district and any past indebt- edness of said school district : Provided , That if there be any sur- plus remaining of said bonds or proceeds thereof or of said taxes , the same shall be turned into the general funds of said school district and shall be used by the trustees for the purpose of meeting the cur- rent expenses of maintaining the schools in said district .

§ 6. Special Tax to Be Discontinued . - That the special tax of four and one - half mills now being levied for the payment of the present existing bonded indebtedness of said school district be dis- continued in case the bonds herein provided for are issued . Approved the 13th day of February , A. D. 1913 .


Year:1913       ACT NO.:161
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE JOHNSTON SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 11 , IN EDGEFIELD COUNTY , TO ISSUE AND SELL COUPON BONDS FOR THE PURPOSE OF ERECTING A PUBLIC SCHOOL BUILDING , AND TO PROVIDE FOR A SINKING FUND COMMISSION AND DEFINE ITS DUTIES .

Section 1. Johnston School District No. 11 Authorized to Issue Bonds . Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina , That the Trustees of Johnston School District No. 11 , in Edgefield county , in the State of South Carolina , are hereby authorized and empowered to issue and sell coupon bonds of the said school district , payable to bearer in such dénominations as they may deem proper , in the amount of twenty - five thousand ( $ 25,000 ) dol- lars , notwithstanding such issue may exceed the four per cent . limi- tation of the assessed valuation of the property of such school dis- trict for taxation , and bearing a rate of interest not exceeding six per centum per annum , payable semiannually on January 1st and July 1st of each year , and at such a place as such trustees deem best : Provided , however , That the entire issue of bonds by said school district , shall not exceed the constitutional eight per centum limita- tion of the assessed valuation of the property of said school district : Provided , further , That the question of issuing the bonds authorized in this section shall be first submitted to the qualified voters of said school district at some time and place in the discretion of the Board of Trustees .

§ 2. Election to Be Ordered . - For the purpose of determining the issuing of bonds authorized in Section 1 of this Act , the trustees of said school district shall order an election to be held at some place in the town of Johnston to be designated by said Board of Trustees , in said school district , on the question of whether such bonds shall be issued or not , in which election only qualified voters residing in such school district shall be allowed to vote , and the trustees shall give notice of such election for ten days in a newspaper published in the county of Edgefield , and by posting said notice in three public places in said school district , and the said Board of Trustees shall designate the time and place , and appoint the managers of such elec- tion , and receive the returns of the managers and declare the results . § 3. Ballots . The ballot cast must have printed on it the words , " For Bonds , " or " Against Bonds . "

§ 4. Issue of Bonds . - If a majority of the votes cast at such election shall be for issuing of bonds , the trustees of said school dis- trict shall issue such bonds , which shall run for not less than twenty nor more than forty years from the date of issue thereof ; which said bonds shall be sold by the Board of Trustees of said school dis- trict , and the proceeds of the sale thereof shall be used by said trustees for the purpose of building a new public school building for said Johnston School District No. 11 , and the said bonds and coupons of the same shall constitute a lien upon the property of the said school district , and it shall be the duty of the county officers of Edgefield county , charged with the assessment and collection of taxes , to levy and collect annually , from all of the property , real and personal , within the limits of said school district , a sum sufficient to pay the interest on said bonds , and also a sum sufficient to provide a sinking fund for the payment of said bonds when due , and the coupons of said bonds shall be received for school taxes upon prop- erty within such district : Provided , That should a majority of the voters in said election be against the issue of bonds , the said Board of Trustees shall not issue the same .

§ 5. Bonds to Be Signed - How . - That all bonds issued under and in pursuance of this Act , shall be signed by the trustees of said school district : Provided , That the signature of such trustees may be lithographed or engraved upon the coupons of such bonds and such lithographed or engraved signatures on said coupons shall be sufficient signing thereof .

§ 6. Proceeds of Sale of Bonds . - The proceeds of such bonds shall be deposited with the County Treasurer of Edgefield county , and shall be receipted for by him and shall be paid out by him only upon the warrant of the Board of Trustees of said school district , as provided by law for the handling , expending and accounting for all other public school funds .

§ 7. Exempt from Taxation . - The said bonds shall be exempt from State , county and municipal taxation .

§ 8. Sinking Fund Commission Created . That the Board of Trustees of Johnston School District No. 11 , in Edgefield county , and their successors in office , be , and they are hereby , created a Sinking Fund Commission for the purpose of handling the sinking fund created under the provisions of this Act for the payment of the said bonds when due . And the said Commission be , and they are hereby , authorized to receive from the hands of the County Treas- urer of Edgefield county , each year , the amount raised by the tax levied under the terms of this Act , in excess of the amount of inter- est on said bonds , and the County Treasurer is hereby authorized and required to pay to said Commission each year the said amount in excess of interest on said bonds , raised by said tax , and take their receipt therefor .

§ 9. Duties of Sinking Fund Commission . - The said Sinking Fund Commission be , and they are hereby , authorized and required to invest such sums as may be received by them from the hands of the County Treasurer on account of the sinking fund created under the provisions of this Act , and the said Commission are authorized to invest said sinking fund in retiring such of the bonds issued under this Act as they may be able to purchase at a fair price , or may lend the said sums on real estate , not exceeding one - half of the appraised value thereof , as appraised by said board , or may lend the said sums to such banks doing business under the laws of this State , as may be approved by the said Board of Trustees . It shall be the duty of said Sinking Fund Commission to have in hand all funds derived under the terms of this Act , at the maturity of said bonds , not already applied to retiring said bonds , and to apply the same to the payment of said bonds . That the said trustees as commissioners of the said sinking fund shall make annual returns of their doings , showing receipts , disbursements , amounts on hand and how invested , to the County Board of Commissioners of Edgefield county , for the year ending December 31st , which report shall be filed on or before the 1st day of March of each year . And that the said trustees as commissioners of the said sinking fund shall give bond in some good · bonding company , authorized to do business in this State , condi- tioned for the faithful performance of their duty , the said bonds to be payable to the County Board of Commissioners of Edgefield county , and to be approved by them , and to be filed with said County Board of Commissioners , the said bond to be each year for the amount of funds in hand at the last report filed by said Sinking Fund Commission .

§ 10. This Act shall take effect upon its approval by the Gov-ernor .


Year:1913       ACT NO.:162
"AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR AN ELECTION ON THE ISSUE OF FIFTY THOUSAND ($50,000) DOLLARS IN COUPON BONDS BY RICHLAND COUNTY FOR THE PURPOSE OF ERECTING A JAIL FOR SAID COUNTY, AND FOR THE ISSUANCE OF SAID BONDS IN CASE THE SAID ELECTION RESULTS
IN FAVOR THEREOF.

Section 1. Bond Election in Richland County for Jail . — Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina , That an election shall be held in the county of Richland on the first Tuesday in April , 1913 , at which election the question of an issue of fifty thousand ( $ 50,000 ) dollars of twenty - year coupon bonds , bear- ing interest at five per cent . , payable semiannually , at such times as shall be designated by the Supervisors and Commissioners herein- after provided for , shall be submitted to the qualified electors of said county .

§ 2. Election . The said election shall be held under the rules . and regulations governing general elections , and the Election Com- missioners shall provide two sets of tickets for the use of the voters at said election , on one set of which shall be printed , " For the Issu- ing of Bonds , " and on the other set shall be printed , " Against Issuing Bonds . "

§ 3. Bonds to Be Issued . If a majority of the votes cast at said election be in favor of the issuing of said bonds , the Supervisor and County Commissioners of Richland county , elected at the last general election , shall issue said coupon bonds for the amount here- inbefore specified .

§ 4. Signature of Bonds . - That said bonds shall be signed by the Supervisor and members of the Board of County Commissioners , who shall affix their official seal thereto , and shall be in the sums of five hundred ( $ 500 ) dollars each . The said Supervisor and Board of County Commissioners shall also sign the coupons of the said bonds in the same manner as the said bonds are signed : Provided , That their names may be lithographed on the said coupons .

§ 5. Sale and Proceeds . - That said bonds shall be sold by the said Supervisor and County Board of Commissioners and the pro- ceeds derived from the said sale shall be used by them in the erection of a jail for Richland county , in the city of Columbia .

§ 6. Annual Tax Levy for Interest and Sinking Fund . - Upon the issuance of said bonds , it shall be the duty of the officers charged with the assessment , levying and collection of taxes , to levy and collect annually from all property , real and personal , within the limits of said county , a sum sufficient to pay the interest on said bonds , and also one - twentieth of the principal , to constitute a sinking fund with which to retire said bonds at maturity ; the same to be paid . over to the County Board of Commissioners to be invested by them for that purpose .

§ 7. Balance of Fund . - If , after the erection and completion of said jail , there remains a balance of said sum unexpended , said bal- ance shall be added to the fund herein provided for the retirement of said bonds at maturity .

§ 8. Election to Be Advertised . That said election shall be advertised for a period of fifteen days in two newspapers printed in the said county prior to the time of the holding of same .

§ 9. Plans and Specifications . - That the said Supervisor and County Board of Commissioners shall employ an architect to draw plans and specifications for said jail and shall advertise for bids for the erection of said jail , in accordance with said plans and specifica- tions . Said bids shall be filed with the Clerk of said Supervisor and Board of Commissioners and shall be opened publicly on the day specified in said advertisement . The said Supervisor and Board of Commissioners shall accept the lowest responsible bid for said work : Provided , That any and all bids may be rejected by the said Super- visor and Board of Commissioners .

§ 10. Bond of Contractor . - Before entering into a contract for the erection of the said jail , the person or persons who shall be awarded the said contract shall enter into a good and sufficient bond in the sum of ten thousand ( $ 10,000 ) dollars , to be approved by the said Supervisor and Board of Commissioners , conditioned for the performance of said contract , according to the plans and specifica- tions submitted by said architect .

§ 11. Inconsistent Acts Repealed . - All Acts or parts of Acts inconsistent with this Act are hereby repealed .

§ 12. Immediately Effective . - This Act shall go into effect . immediately upon its approval by the Governor .


Year:1913       ACT NO.:177
AN ACT TO INCORPORATE GREENWOOD EDUCATIONAL ASSOCIATION, OF GREENWOOD, S. C.

Section 1. Greenwood Educational Association Incorporated.— Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina (a Concurrent Resoution, allowing this Bill to be intro- duced, having been passed by a two-thirds vote of each House, as required by the Constitution), That H. V. R. Schrader, F. N. K. Bailey, A. F. McKissick, D. A. G. Ouzts, W. T. Jones. C. C. Featherstone, S. C. Hodges, W. J. Snead and Kenneth Baker, of Greenwood, S. C., trustees, and their successors in office, be, and are hereby, created and constituted a body politic and corporate, under the name and style of “Greenwood Educational Associ- 7 ation,’ and as such corporation and in, by and under the said name shall have the right to contract and be contracted with, to sue and be sued and in any manner whatsoever, to acquire, hold and dispose of any and all kinds of property, real, personal and mixed, and to lease or mortgage the same; to have and use a com- mon seal, to make such by-laws, rules and regulations as may be thought proper and, generally, to have all such rights, powers and privileges as are usually incident to corporations of like char- acter and as now are or hereafter may be conferred by gencral laws upon corporations organized for educational purposes and as may not be repugnant to the Constitution and laws of this State or of the United States. 

§ 2. Power to Establish and Maintain School.—That the said corporation shall have, and it is hereby given, the power to establish, maintain and operate at or near the town of Green- wood, in the State of South Carolina, a high grade school or cvl- lege, for the liberal education of white boys and men, and for these purposes shall be authorized to do all such acts and make all such contracts as may be proper or necessary. 

§ 3. Board of Trustees——That all the powers given said cor- poration shall be, and they are hereby, lodged in a Board of Trus- tees, consisting of the persons named in Section 1 of this Act. and such other persons as may be substituted for them, or any of them, or chosen to succeed them, or any of them, in the manner hereinafter provided. That three of the members of the said Board of Trustees shall hold office for the term of one year, or until their successors are elected; that two of the members of the said Board of Trustees shall hold office for the term of two years, or until their successors are elected ; that two of the mem- bers of the said Board of Trustees shall hold office for the term of three years, or until their successors are elected, and that two of the members of the Board of Trustees shall hold office for the term of four years, or until their successors are elected; that the said trustees, named in this Act, shall determine by lot which of them shall hold for one year, two years, three years and four years, and thereafter there shall be held annually, at such time and place as may be fixed by the by-laws, an election, at which the successors of the said trustees so named in Section 1 of this Act, shall be elected. 

§ 4. Certificates of Stock.—That the said corporation shall issue to such person or persons as shall or may hereafter subscribe money or other property to said corporation for the purpose of establishing, improving or maintaining the same, certificates, show- ing the amount or amounts contributed by them, the said contri- butions or certificates to be divided into shares of fifty dollars each, and the said certificates to show the number of shares con- tributed by each person or persons; that the said contributors shall, for the purpose of electing the said trustees, be deemed to be stockholders in the said corporation and the said annual meet- ing, heretofore provided for, shall be composed of the said stock- holders, and in the election of the said trustees each stockholder shall be entitled to one vote for each share of stock so held by him or her, and it shall take only a majority of the shares repre- sented at the meeting to elect said trustees: Provided, That at said meeting the said stockholders may vote in person or by proxy, as now provided by law with reference to meetings of stockholders in other corporations: Provided, That the provision of this section shall not apply to donations of land or property for a site, or otherwise. 

§ 5. Degrees.—That the said corporation shall have power and authority to confer and award all such distinctions, honors and degrees as are usually conferred or awarded by any of the col- leges and universities of the United States. § 6. Property to Be Used for Educational Purposes.—That all of the property, real, personal or mixed, held by the said corpora- tion shall be used only for educational purposes, at or near the town of Greenwood, in the State of South Carolina, and in the event that the said property should, for any reason, cease to be used for such educational purposes, at or near the said place, the said corporation shall be dissolved and all of the assets of the said corporation shall revert to the said stockholders, or their assignees, and the same shall be distributed by the said trustees to the said stockholders, or their assignees, in proportion to the several amounts owned by them. 

§ 7. Charter in Perpetuity—The charter herein granted shall be held in perpetuity unless said corporation shall be dissolved which said dissolution may be brought about by a two-thirds vote of the said stockholders, in a meeting called for that pur- pose, of which thirty days’ notice shall be given to the said stock- holders, in writing, by mail or in person: Provided, That at such meeting, and in all meetings of the said stockholders, the vote shall be taken by stock, each stockholder being entitled to one vote for each share of stock represented by him or her 

§ 8. Exempt from Taxation.—That all of the property owned by the said corporation, real, personal or mixed, shall be used so long as the corporation exists, for educational purposes, and for said purposes only, and all of the said property of the said corporation, so long as it shall be used for educational purposes shall be exempt from the State, county and municipal taxes 

§ 9. May Borrow Money.—That the said corporation shall, if a majority of its trustees deem it wise, have full power and authority to borrow money for the purpose of erecting or improv- ing its buildings, or plant, and to pledge or mortgage its prop- erty, real or personal, to secure the payment of said money so borrowed. 

§ 10. Immediately Effective-—That this Act shall be deemed and taken to be a public Act, and shall go into effect and con- tinue of force from and immediately after the day of its approval.

AN ACT TO RATIFY THE AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE X OF THE CONSTITUTION OF 1895, BY ADDING THERETO SECTION 14A, TO EMPOWER THE CITIES OF CHARLESTON AND BEAUFORT TO ASSESS ABUTTING PROPERTY FOR PERMANENT IMPROVEMENTS. 

 AN ACT to Ratify the Amendment to Article X of the Constitu- tion of 1895, by Adding Thereto Section 14a, to Empower the Cities of Charleston and Beaufort to Assess Abutting Property for Permanent Improvements. Whereas, The General Assembly did, by Joint Resolution pre- sented to the Governor the sixteenth day of February, A. D. 1912, and not returned by him to the House in which it originated within three days, the General Assembly being in session, submit to the qualified electors of the State, at the general election next thereafter, an amendment to Article X of the Constitution of the State of South Carolina, by adding thereto Section 14a, as follows: Section 14a. The General Assembly may authorize the corporate authorities of the cities of Charleston and Beaufort to !evy an assess- ment upon abutting property for the purpose of paying for perma- nent improvements on streets and sidewalks immediately abutting 

such property: Provided, That said improvements be ordered only upon the written consent of two-thirds of the owners of the property abutting upon the street, sidewalk, or part of either proposed to be improved, and upon condition that said corporate authorities shall pay at least one-half of the costs of such improvements ; and, Whereas, A majority of the electors qualified to vote for members of the General Assembly, voting thereon at the general election next succeeding the passage of the Joint Resolution, did vote in favor of said amendment ; therefore, Section 1. Cities of Charleston and Beaufort Allowed to Assess Abutting Property.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That amendment to Article X of the Constitution of the State of South Carolina, whereby Section 14a was added thereto, submitted by the last General Assembly to the qualified electors of the State at the general election next thereafter, and upon which a majority of the electors qualified to vote for members of the General Assembly, voting thereon at the last general election voted in favor thereof, be, and the same is hereby, ratified and made a part of the Constitution of the State of South Carolina ; that the said amendment so made a part of the said Constitution is as follows: Section 14a. The General Assembly may authorize the corporate authorities of the cities of Charleston and Beaufort to levy an assessment upon abutting property for the purpose of paying for permanent improvements on streets and sidewalks immediately abut- ting such property: Provided, That said improvements be ordered only upon the written consent of two-thirds of the owners of the property abutting upon the street, sidewalk, or part of either, to be improved, and upon condition that said corporate authorities shall pay at least one-half of the costs of such improvements. Article X, § 14a, Constitution 1905. . * k * This Act was presented to the Governor the 19th day of February, A. D. 1913, and was not returned by him to the House in which it originated within three days, the General Assembly being in session. —Code Commissioner.

Year:1913       ACT NO.:202
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE SCHOOL TRUSTEES OF THE AIKEN SCHOOL TO ERECT A NEW SCHOOL BUILDING AND TO PROVIDE FOR RAISING FUNDS FOR THE SAME.

Whereas, The Aiken Institute, the graded school of School District No. 1, of Aiken county, is controlled by a Board of Trustees composed of the Directors of the Aiken Institute. a corporation, and the trustees of said school district, and sup- ported by the school funds of said school district, and tuition fees, according to certain Acts of the General Assembly of South Carolina passed during the year 1890 and 1891; and, Whereas, It is necessary to accommodate the increased number of scholars in said school district that another school building should be erected: Section 1. Trustees of Aiken School Authorized to Erect New Building.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That the Trustees of Aiken School District No. 1, which embraces the corporate limits of the city of Aiken. be. and they are hereby, authorized and empowered and directed to appropriate five thousand dollars out of the surplus fund of said school district, which they have on hand during the year 

1912, towards the erection of such needed additional school build- ing, to be used along with two thousand dollars now held by the Trustees of the Aiken Institute for the erection of said building. § 2. May Execute Mortgage to Raise Funds.—That an addi- tional school building be erected upon the lot owned by the Aiken Institute at such place on said lot and of such size and dimen- sions as shall be fixed by the Board of Trustees governing said Aiken Institute ; and inasmuch as it is estimated that said needed building will cost at least twenty thousand dollars, and there are no other school funds available than the aforesaid amounts, the stockholders of said corporation, the Aiken Institute, by a majority vote in a meeting called for said purpose, are hereby authorized and empowered to empower the trustees who manage said school to mortgage said lot, together with the building now thereon and the other building to be built for the purpose of raising so much of the additional fund as may be needed; and said authority is given, notwithstanding the fact that the deeds upon which said property are held prescribe that the property shall be held for school purposes only, and to the extent of said mortgage given for said purpose, only said property is hereby declared (if said stockholders so direct) to be free from said limitations for said purpose. § 3. Payment of Mortgage—How.—That in order to provide for the payment of said mortgage so authorized as aforesaid, the School Trustees of said Graded School District No. 1, of Aiken County, be, and they are hereby, authorized and empow- ered and required to pay upon said mortgage from year to year any surplus that may be to their credit as School Trustees in the treasury of Aiken county; and the Treasurer of said county shall recognize and pay their warrant therefor. § 4. City Council May Release Property from Lien.—That the City Council of Aiken by a majority vote be, and they are hereby. authorized and empowered to release the property of the said Aiken Institute, which is to be covered by the aforesaid mort- gage, so as to allow the lien of said mortgage from any claim which they may be advised that they may have, because of bonds previously issued by the said city of Aiken under Section 4 of Act No. 771 of the General Assembly of South Carolina, approved December 16, 1891, and entitled “An Act to authorize the city of Aiken to issue bonds in aid of the Aiken Institute.” 

§ 5. Bond Election—Proviso.—That in case the trustees in charge of the aforesaid graded school fail to negotiate the mort- gage authorized as aforesaid within any reasonable time after the passage of this Act, and shall certify the same to the trustees of said Aiken School District No. 1, then, and in that event, said Trustees of Aiken School District No. 1 be, and they are hereby. authorized and empowered, after giving public notice once a week for four weeks in one of the newspapers published in the city of Aiken, to call an election of the qualified electors of said Aiken School District No. 1 to vote upon the question of the issuing, by said Aiken School District No. 1, of thirteen thousand dollars of bonds of said district, to be used for the purpose of the erection of said additional building for said graded school; that the said Trustees of said Aiken School District are authorized and empowered to appoint the managers for said election and the time and place for holding of the same, which said election shall be held under the rules and regulation of the Constitution and Statutes of the State of South Carolina in regard to General Elections, except that the production of a registration certificate by the registration officers of Aiken county for the precinct of Aiken shall be sufficient without the use of the registration book for said precinct, but that the elector must reside within the territory of said School District No. 1, and that the said trustees must furnish for the use of the voters in said election an equal number of- ballots, on one set of which shall be printed the words, “For the Issuing of Bonds,” and on the other set the words, ‘Against the Issuing of Bonds,” and a sufficient number of ballots shall be placed at the usual place of voting on the day of election. That the managers as aforesaid to be appointed shall conduct the said election, and at the close thereof shall canvass the vote and make return thereof in writing to the trustees aforesaid. who shall act thereon, and certify to the same to the Clerk of Court of Aiken county for filing in his office. § 6. Bond Issue.—That if at said election a majority of the votes declare for the issuing of bonds, the said Board of Trustees of the said School District shall issue the same up to the amount of $13,000, if so much be necessary, to run for a period of not more than forty years, with the right to redeem the same after twenty years; said bonds to draw not greater than seven per cent. per annum, but to be issued at a lower rate if they can be sold at par; and the said trustees are authorized to sell said bonds and appropriate 

the proceeds of said sale along with the Directors of the Aiken Institute with the funds as specified as aforesaid for the election of the additional school building on the lot as aforesaid to be a part of the graded school property in the city of Aiken. § 7. Bonds.—That the said bonds and the coupons thereof shall be signed by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees and counter- signed by the Secretary of the Board of Trustees of said Aiken School District No. 1: Provided, That the signatures of the said officers on said coupons may be lithographed and that the said lithographing shall be sufficient signing of the bonds and coupons. § 8. Annual Tax Levy to Pay Interest.—That upon the order of the trustees and their successors in office, it shall be the duty of the county officers, charged with the assessment and collection of taxes of Aiken county, to levy and collect annually from the property of said school district a sum sufficient to pay the interest on said school bonds; and also a sum to provide for a sinking fund for the payment of the said sum when due, the amount of said taxes to be designated and certified to said trustees, and said Board of Trustees to pay the said coupons as they mature. § 8. Exempt from Taxation.—That the bonds issued under this Act shall be exempt from taxation—State, county and municipal. § 10. AN ACT RELATING TO SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 52, OF NEWBERRY COUNTY. 

Section 1. Bond Issue for School District No. 52, in Newberry County.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That for the purpose of enlarging and equipping the school building of School District No. 52, of Newberry county, the trustees of said school district are hereby authorized and empowered to issue coupon bonds to the amount of five thousand ($5,000) dollars, if so much be necessary, for said pur- pose, payable in twenty years and bearing interest at not exceed- ing six per centum per annum, payable semiannually: Provided, That at an election to be held hereafter a majority of the quali- fied electors of said school district voting shall be in favor of the issue of said school bonds. § 2. Notice of Election—That the trustees of said school dis- trict are hereby required to give two weeks’ previous nqtice by publication in one or more of the newspapers published in New- berry county, and by posting at three public places in said school district, of the time and place of such election. § 38. Denominations of Bonds, etc.—That the said bonds shall be issued in such denominations as the trustees may fix, and 

shall be signed by the trustees, but the signatures of the trustees may be lithographed on the coupons attached to said bonds. Said bonds shall be exempt from taxation for State, county and municipal purposes. The coupons attached to said bonds shall be receivable in payment of any taxes due said school district. § 4. Annual Tax Levy to Pay Interest, etc.—That for the pur- pose of paying the interest on said bonds and providing a sink- ing fund for the payment of the principal of said bonds, the Audi- tor of Newberry county, or such other officer as may be charged with the assessment of taxes, shall annually levy a tax of three- fourths (34) of one mill on all the taxable property in said school district, and the tax so levied shall be collected by the County Treasurer of Newberry county as State and county taxes are col- lected, to be held and applied by him for said purposes only, viz., to the payment of the interest on said bonds, and the surplus after paying the interest each year as a sinking fund for the pay- ment of the principal of said bonds, which surplus shall be depos- ited at interest by the County Treasurer under the direction of the trustees of said school district. § 5. Proceeds of Bonds.—That the trustees of said school dis- trict shall use said bonds or the proceeds of the sale thereof at not less than par value for the purposes mentioned in Section 1 of this Act, any surplus to be turned into the general funds of said school district and used for maintaining and equipping the schools of the district. § 6. Bonds to Be Registered in Office County Superintendent Education.—Said bonds shall be registered in the office of the County Superintendent of Education. § 7. Immediately Effective—This Act shall go into effect immediately. * * * This Act was presented to the Governor the 21st day of Feb- ruary, A. D, 1913, and was not returned by him to the House in which it originated within three days, the General Assembly being in session.—Code Commissioner. 

No. 215. AN ACT Relating to Newberry School District. Section 1. Election for Newberry School District—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That the Trustees of Newberry School District are hereby author- ized and empowered to submit to the qualified electors of said school district not later than July 15th, 1913, the question of levying an additional tax of one mill on the taxable property in said school district, to be used for improvements and repairs. § 2. Trustees to Order Election.—Said trustees, if they deem it necessary to hold an election on this question, shall order said election on not less than full four weeks’ notice thereof, published in the newspapers of said school district, stating the time and place of voting. They shall appoint three managers to conduct the election, prescribe the form of ballots, receive the written returns from the managers showing the votes cast for and against the levy of said tax and declare the result of the election. § 3. Assessment of Tax.—In case the majority of the votes cast is in favor of the said tax levy, the trustees shall certify the fact to the County Auditor, who shall thereupon assess said tax on the taxable property of said district and enter the same upon the tax duplicate. The County Treasurer shall thereupon collect said tax at the same time and in the same manner as other taxes. § 4. Account of Tax.—The County Treasurer shall keep a sep- arate account of said tax and pay out the same on the warrants of the trustees issued for the purposes aforesaid. § 5. Levy for 1918 and 1914.—Said tax, if voted, shall be levied for the fiscal years 1913 and 1914, only any surplus of said tax, after providing for the improvements and repairs contemplated by the trustees, may be used by them for the current main- tenance of the schools in said district. § 6. Trustees May Borrow Money.—The trustees of said dis- trict are authorized to borrow money on account of said tax, if voted for the purpose of making improvements and repairs and to pledge said tax for the payment of such money as they may borrow. AN ACT to Amend Section 1730 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina, 1912, Volume I, Relating to the Compensation of Members of the County Board of Education of Kershaw County. Section 1.—Compensation County Board of Education Kershaw County.—BDe it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That Section 1730 of the Code of Laws of South Carolina, 1912, Volume I, be amended by adding to the end thereof the following: Provided, That the two members of the County 

OF SOUTH CAROLINA. 301 Board of Education for Kershaw county shall receive three dollars per diem for not exceeding twelve days and mileage as now provided by law, so that said section, when so amended, shall read as follows: Section 1730. The County Board of Education shall examine all candidates for the position of teacher, and give to each person found qualifted a certificate setting forth the branches of learning he or she may be capable of teaching, and the percentage attained in each branch, said certificate to be valid for a term of two years, unless sooner revoked, and it may be renewed with or without examination, at the discretion of the Board, all of which shall be done under such regulations as the State Board of Education may prescribe. No teacher shall be employed in any of the free public schools with- out a certificate from the County Board of Education or the State Board of Education: Provided, That no examination as to the qualification shall be made in case of any applicant who produces a full diploma from any chartered college or university of this State, or Memminger Normal School, of Charleston, and furnish satisfactory evidence of good moral character: Provided, further, That the State Board of Education shall examine into the curricu- lum, standing, faculty and equipment of each institution, and see that it is doing real college work, before certificates may be issued on its diplomas. The two members of the Board appointed by the State Board of Education shall receive for the services rendered by them compensation at the rate of three dollars per diem for not exceeding seven days. except in the counties of Greenville and Orangeburg, where the number of days shall not exceed twenty; and in the counties of Barnwell, Dorchester, York and Hampton, where the number of days shall be ten, if so much be necessary, in each year, and mileage of five cents for each mile of necessary travel, the same to be paid by the County Board of Commissioners out of the ordinary school funds: Provided, That the two members of the County Board of Education for Kershaw county shall receive three dollars per diem for not exceeding twelve days and mileage as now provided by law. AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION 104, VOLUME II, CODE OF LAWS, 1912,
RELATING TO ABLE -BODIED MALE CONVICTS , SO AS TO INCLUDE THE
COUNTY OF GREENVILLE IN ITS PROVISIONS . 

AN ACT to Amend Section 104, Volume II, Code of Laws, 1912, Relating to Able-bodied Male Convicts, so as to Include the County of Greenville in Its Provisions. Section 1. Convicts to Work Roads in Greenville—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina, That Section 104 of the Criminal Code, 1912, be, and the same is hereby, amended by striking out the words “counties of Greenville and,” on line 11 of said section, and inserting in lieu thereof the words “county of,” so that when said section is so amended it shall read as follows: Section 104. Able-bodied Male Convicts to Work on County Chain Gangs, Proviso and Exceptions—In every case in which imprisonment is provided as the punishment, in whole or in part, for 

516 STATUTES AT LARGE . crime, all able-bodied male convicts shall hereafter be sentenced to hard labor on the public works of the county in which convicted. if such county maintains a chain gang, without regard to the length of sentence, and in the alternative to imprisonment in the county jail or the State Penitentiary at hard labor: Provided, That in any case the presiding Judge shall have the power, by special order, to direct that any person convicted before him be confined in the State Peniten- tiary, if it is considered unsafe or unwise for such convict to be com- mitted to county chain gang: Provided, That the provisions of this Act shall not apply to the county of Clarendon: Provided, That a separation of the sexes and races be at all times observed, except in the penitentiary and on the State farm in Kershaw county: Provided, further, Should the Supervisor or Commissioner of any county find that it is inconvenient or impracticable to work any convict com- mitted to the county chain gang, he may turn said convict over to the penitentiary authorities. Criminal Code 1912, § 104. Approved

AN ACT TO AMEND AN ACT ENTITLED "AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR
THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A NEW TOWNSHIP AND SCHOOL DISTRICT
IN CHESTER COUNTY , AND TO AUTHORIZE THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF A LOCAL TAX THEREIN ," ENACTED BY THE GENERAL
ASSEMBLY IN 1879 , AS AMENDED BY ACTS AMENDATORY
THEREOF, APPROVED DECEMBER 20 , 1893 , AND FEBRUARY 23 ,
1910 .
 

Section 1. New Township and School District in Chester County - Amendment . - Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina , That an Act entitled " An Act to pro- vide for the establishment of a new township and school district in Chester county , and to authorize the levy and collection of a local tax therein , " enacted by the General Assembly in 1879 , as amended by Acts amendatory thereof , approved December 20 , 1893 , and February 23 , 1910 , and all other Acts amendatory thereof , be , and the same is hereby , amended by striking out on line seven of Section 3 of said Act as amended ( as the same appears on page 891 , XXVI , Statutes at Large ) the words " January next , " and inserting in lieu thereof the word and figures " March , 1914 , " and by striking out on the next line of said section the word , letters and figures , " October , A. D. 1880 , " and inserting in lieu thereof the word , letters and figures , " March , A. D. 1915 , " so that said section , when amended , shall read as follows :

Section 2. The said school district is also hereby authorized and empowered to levy on all real and personal property returned in said district a local tax , not exceeding four mills on the dollar , to supplement the constitutional tax for support of said schools by the persons and in the mode following , to wit : The School Trustees of said district shall on or before the 15th day of March , 1914 , and again on or before the 1st day of March , A. D. 1915 , and on or before the last named day in each succeeding year , call a meeting of all the legal voters living in said district and returning real or personal property therein ; that a notice of said meeting , specifying the time , place and object thereof , shall be published in one newspaper or more in the said district , and posted on the courthouse door and at the postoffice therein , at least ten days before the said meeting . The persons answering the above designation , when thus assembled , shall appoint a Chairman and Secretary , adjourn from time to time , decide what additional tax , if any , shall be levied , and appropriate the same in such manner as they may think best for maintaining said school . No tax thus levied shall be repealed at a subsequent meeting held within the same fiscal year . The Chairman of the said meeting shall in one week thereafter notify the Chairman of the Board of Trustees and the County Auditor of the amount of the tax thus levied , and how it has been appropriated , and the County Auditor shall at once assess such tax on all real and personal property returned in said district or township , and the County Treasurer shall collect the same with the State and county tax ; and it shall be a lien on all property till paid , and defaulting taxpayers shall be liable to like process and penalties as defaulters for State and county taxes . The money collected from said tax levy shall be paid out by the County Treasurer for purposes to which it has been appropriated , on warrants drawn by the Trustees of said dis- trict , countersigned by the County School Commissioner ; and said Treasurer shall be liable to said school district for non- performance of his duty in respect to said moneys in same . manner and under like penalties as for nonperformance of his duty in reference to State and county taxes . The first assess- ment under this Act shall be for the scholastic year beginning on 1st of November , 1879. This Act shall take effect from the date of its passage , and all Acts inconsistent therewith are hereby repealed .
