Year:1916       ACT NO.:577
AN ACT TO CANCEL ALL PREVIOUS REGISTRATIONS AND TO PROVIDE FOR THE REREGISTRATION OF THE QUALIFIED ELECTORS OF BEAUFORT COUNTY.

Section 1. Previous Registrations Canceled.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That 

from and after the passage of this Act, all previous registration of electors of Beaufort County be and the same are hereby can- celled and made and void. § 2. Provisions for New Registration.—That immediately after the passage of this Act it shall be the duty of the Board of Reg- istration of Beaufort County to open the Books of registration and register the qualified electors of Beaufort County commenc- ing a new series of numbers of the certificates of registration and for the purpose of enabling all the electors of Beaufort County to qualify and register and obtain registration certificates they are hereby required to open such books of registration at each polling place from the hours of Nine A. M. to Two P. M. and Four P. M. to Six P. M. on each day for the number of days hereinafter specified or required. § 3. Notice of Opening of Books to Be Given.—The said Board of Registration immediately upon the passage of this Act shall advertise in the Beaufort Gazette the time of opening the books of registration at each polling place in said county for not less than two weeks before opening said books at each polling place and shall keep the same open during the hours above mentioned and specified in Section 2 of this Act for a period of Ten days at Beaufort, Six days at Bluffton and Four days at Hardeeville and Two days at each of the other polling precincts in said county. § 4. Entries to Be Made.—It shall be the duty of the said Board of Registration to enter in the Books of Registration the serial number and date of each certificate issued and of each reissue thereafter and also the age, color and occupation of each elector at the time of such registration and of any subsequent reissue of a registration certificate. § 5. Issue of Duplicate Certificates.—Whenever a renewal of certificate is issued by reason of loss or destruction of the orig- inal, such renewal shall be a duplicate and bear the serial num- ber of the original and have printed across its face the word “Duplicate.” § 6. Immediately Effective—This Act shall go into effect immediately upon its approval by the Governor. 


Year:1916       ACT NO.:579
AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE SUBMISSION TO THE QUALIFIED ELECTORS OF THE TOWN OF BLUFFTON OF THE REPEAL OF THE CHARTER OF SAID TOWN AND TO PROVIDE FOR WINDING UP THE AFFAIRS THEREOF IN THE EVENT THE RESULT OF SAID VOTE SHALL BE IN FAVOR OF THE REPEAL OF SAID CHARTER.

 Section 1. Election to Decide Charter Repeal for Bluffton Provided.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That the Intendant and Wardens of the Town of Bluffton be and they are hereby required within ten days after the approval of this Act to order an election to be held as are other elections in said town, for the purpose of submitting to the qualified electors of said town the question of the repeal of the charter of incorporation of said town. § 2. Reregistration of Electors Required.—For the purpose of providing for a full and fair expression of the will of the people said Intendant and Wardens are required to provide for a reregistration of all the qualified electors within the corporate limits of said town in the manner provided by law and to hold said election not earlier than six, nor later than eight weeks after the date of ordering said election. § 3. Ballots—How Marked.—At said election the qualified electors shall cast ballots on which shall be printed “FOR AGAINST repeal of Charter,” which ballots shall be provided by said Intendant and Wardens for all voters. All those desir- ing to vote for repeal of the charter shall cross out the word “AGAINST” and all those desiring to vote to retain the charter shall cross out the word “FOR” before depositing their ballots. § 4. Procedure After Election—How Municipality May Be Wound Up.—If a majority of the votes cast at said election be against the repeal of the charter the Intendant-Wardens shall certify the result of said election the Legislative Delegation from Beaufort County and proceed with the Town Government as if no election had been held. If a majority of the votes cast at said election shall be in favor of the repeal of said charter then the said Intendant and Wardens shall certify the same to the Legislative Delegation from Beaufort County and shall forthwith cease to exercise any of the powers of municipal officers except for the purpose of winding up the affairs of said town which they shall do in the following manner: They shall 

OS cause to be paid to each municipal officer his salary at the rate existing at the time of the passage of this Act, up to ten days after said election; they shall pay up all outstanding indebted- ness of said town; they shall advertise for sale, by posting notices for at least six days in three or more prominent places in said town, all the personal property of said town except the books of account and records and documents, and sell the said personal property at public outcry for cash to the highest bidder and shall then disburse all funds remaining in manner follow- ing, to wit: By paying back to each licensee of said town the unearned proportion of the license money paid by him and then pay back to the taxpayers of said town, their agents or legal representatives all taxes paid by them during the last tax paying period, and if the fund is insufficient for that purpose then the same must be paid in the proportion that such fund bears to the whole amount of taxes collected. They shall then turn over to the County Commissioners of Beaufort County the books of account, records and documents of said town and all remaining cash, and the wharf and all real estate of said town, to be by said County Commissioners held as custodians until such further disposition may be made thereof by the General Assembly as it may determine. § 5. Charter Repeal Effective May 6, 1916, Unless Electors Vote Otherwise—County Commissioners to Wind Up Affairs if Municipal Officers Fail to Do So.—The Charter of the Town of Bluffton is hereby repealed to take effect on the 6th day of May, A. D. 1916, unless the provisions of Sections 1, 2 and 3 of this Act are complied with; but if said provisions of this Act are complied with the charter is repealed to take effect on said date if the result of the election shall be in favor of the repeal of said charter but not otherwise. If the provisions of Sections 1, 2 and 3 of this Act are not complied with the said Intendant and Wardens are hereby prohibited from drawing out any of the funds of said town, as salary or otherwise, and the duties imposed upon them by Section 4 of this Act for the pur- pose of winding up the affairs of said town shall be performed by the County Commissioners of the County of Beaufort or by some person named by them for that purpose, whose compensa- tion shall be fixed by the said County Commissioners and paid out of the municipal funds of said town. 


Year:1916       ACT NO.:612
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE AND EMPOWER WINYAH INDIGO SCHOOL DISTRICT OF GEORGETOWN COUNTY TO ISSUE COUPON BONDS FOR THE PURPOSE OF ALTERING, ENLARGING AND EQUIPPING BUILDINGS FOR THE PUBLIC SCHOOLS OF SAID DISTRICT, AND TO PROVIDE FOR THE PAYMENT OF THE SAME.

Section 1. Bond Issue for School Purposes Authorized—Elec- tion Prerequisite——Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That Winyah Indigo School Dis- trict, of Georgetown County, is hereby authorized and empow- ered to issue coupon bonds to the amount of fifteen thousand < dollars, or so much thereof as may, in the judgment of the Board of Trustees of said district, be necessary, for the purpose of altering, enlarging and equipping any existing public school building or buildings in the city of Georgetown, in said district: Provided, That the question of issuing said bonds shall first be determined at a special election to be held for that purpose, as hereinafter provided, in which a majority of the qualified electors voting thereat shall vote in favor of such issue. 
§ 2. Election—Notice—Ballot—That upon the written peti- tion of one-fourth of the resident freeholders of said school dis- trict, filed with the said Trustees, they shall make an order for the holding of such an election, fixing the time and place for holding the same, appointing the managers (who shall be three resident freeholders and qualified electors of said district), and making At such all other proper provisions for the conduct thereof. At such

election only duly qualified electors residing in said district shall be entitled to vote. The said Trustees shall publish, at least twenty days prior to the holding of said election, in one or more newspapers published in the city of Georgetown, due notice of the time and place of holding same, and of the objects thereof, in which shall be specified the amount of bonds proposed to be issued, the time when the same shall become payable and the rate of interest thereon. The Trustees shall have printed, for the use of the voters in said election, an equal number of ballots for and against said issue, on one set of which shall be printed the words, “For the issuing of bonds,” and on the other set the words, “Against the issuing of bonds,” and a sufficient number of such ballots shall be placed at the following place or places in said district on the day of election. The said managers shall conduct the election, and at the close thereof shall count the votes and make a return of the result thereof in writing to the Board of School Trustees aforesaid. The said Trustees shall canvass the returns and declare the result; and if a majority of the bal- lots cast at such election shall be in favor of the issue of said bonds, the said Board of Trustees shall proceed to issue and dis- pose of the same as hereinafter provided. § 3. Bonds—Denominations—Interest—Are Lien.—That the said bonds shall be of such denominations as may be determined by the said Trustees, shall bear interest at a rate not exceeding five per centum per annum, payable either annually or semi- annually, and the principal thereof shall be due and payable thirty years from and after the date thereof with the right of redemption after twenty years from said date. Both principal and interest of said bonds shall be payable in any legal tender money of the United States. Each of said bonds and interest coupons attached thereto shall be signed by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of said school district, and countersigned by the Secretary of said Board: Provided, That the signature of said officers may be lithographed in facsimile upon the bonds and coupons, and such lithographing shall be a sufficient proof of the execution thereof under the terms of this Act. The said bonds when duly issued in conformity to the provisions of this Act, shall, in the hands of any bona fide holder for value, con- stitute a lien upon all property altered, enlarged and equipped with the proceeds of the sale thereof. § 4. Sale - Deposit - Disbursement - Bond - Duties . - That the said bonds shall be sold by the Board of Trustees at either pub-

lic or private sale, as in their judgment may be best; but no such sale shall be made at less than par and accrued interest. The proceeds of such sale shall be paid over by the said Board of Trustees to the County Treasurer of the County of George- town, who shall keep a separate account thereof and shall hold the same subject to the orders of the said Board, and pay them out upon warrants duly issued by said Board in like manner as other public school funds belonging to said district. The County Treasurer shall be liable upon his official bond to the said school district, or to any party interested, for the non- performance of his duty in respect to said fund in the same manner and to the same extent and under like penalty as to non- performance of his duties in reference to other public moneys entrusted to his keeping: Provided, however, That the said Board of Trustees may, in their discretion deposit the said funds in the usual depository for State or County funds, in the name of the said school district, subject to their own order, and dis- burse the same directly by check or draft thereon, signed by the Chairman and countersigned by the Secretary of the Board: Provided, further, That before the said Board shall exercise the power of deposit and direct disbursement of said funds herein granted to it, each of said Trustees shall enter into bond in the sum of two thousand five hundred dollars with security, to be approved by the County Board of Commissioners, conditioned for the faithful performance of their official duties. The pre- mium, which may be paid to any surety or guarantee company for “i furnishing said official bonds, and all other expenses which may be in the issue and sale of the bonds authorized by this Act, shall be paid by the said Trustees from the proceeds of the sale of such bonds or from any other fund of said school district. And the said Board of Trustees shall apply and expend all of said funds exclusively for the purposes provided in this Act. § 5. Exempt from Taxation.—That the said bonds and the coupons thereto attached shall be exempt from taxation in this State. § 6. Disposition of Surplus.—That, if there shall remain any surplus funds from the proceeds of the sale of the said bonds after carrying out the purposes of this Act, and the payment of all expenses incident thereto, the same shall be covered into the county Treasury and shall constitute a part of the sinking 

fund to be created, as hereinafter provided, for the retirement of the said bonds. § 7. Tax Levy—Sinking Fund.—That for the purpose of pay- ing annual interest upon the said bonds, and of establishing a sinking fund for the retirement of the same at maturity or at the period of redemption, it shall be the duty of the County Auditor or of such other officers as may be charged by law with the levy and assessment of taxes, to levy annually such a tax upori all the taxable real and personal property in the said school dis- trict as shall be sufficient to meet the said interest, and also to raise a sum equal to one-fortieth (1-40) of the principal of said bonds, to be held as a sinking fund for that purpose. The amount so levied shall be collected by the County Treasurer of said County in like manner as State, County and school taxes are collected, and shall be applied by him solely to the payment of the said interest or of the principal of said bonds, respectively, and shall be used for no other purpose whatsoever. § 8. Place of Deposit—Redemption.—That it shall be the duty of the County Treasurer to place all monies belonging to the sinking funds hereinbefore provided for on deposit in some savings bank in this State, to be designated in writing jointly by the said Board of Trustees and the County Auditor, and all interest accruing thereon shall be likewise kept on deposit in such savings bank. That when the right of redemption shall arise, at the expiration of the period of twenty years, as fixed by this Act, the said County Treasurer shall be authorized and he is hereby directed, at the written request of the said Board of Trustees, through its Chairman and Secretary, to redeem the said bonds, or so many thereof as the sinking fund may be sufficient to pay; and the remainder of said issue, if any, may be redeemed from time to time thereafter at the option of said Board of Trustees, in such amounts as may be deemed expedient by them, and the Board may designate the bonds to be so 7 redeemed. § 9. Inconsistent Acts Repealed—That this Act shall take effect immediately upon its approval; and all other Acts or parts of Acts inconsistent herewith are hereby repealed.

Year:1916       ACT NO.:625
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE SCHOOL TRUSTEES OF LANCASTER SCHOOL DISTRICT TO HOLD AN ELECTION ON THE QUESTION OF MAINTAINING A PUBLIC LIBRARY, BY AN ANNUAL TAX OF ONE-
HALF OF ONE MILL.

Whereas, Mr. Andrew Carnegie proposes to devote not less than six thousand dollars to the erection of a public library within Lancaster School District, No. 14, of Lancaster county, upon conditions that the town of Lancaster, or citizens thereof, furaish a lot therefor, free of cost, and the School District supply the funds for maintenance of the same; now, therefore, Section 1. Election for Public Library Authorized.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That said School Trustees, upon a petition of a majority of the freeholders of said school district, in that behalf, be and are hereby authorized and empowered and required to hold an elec- tion on the question of an annual levy of one-half of one mill, on all the property returned in said district for taxation, for the maintenance of a public library therein; said election shall be held on a day to be fixed by said Trustees, after three weeks’ au advertisement in a newspaper published at Lancaster, at which election all qualified electors of said district, shall be entitled - “~~ to vote. 
§ 2. Form of Ballot.—The said Trustees shall furnish a suffi- cient and equal number of ballots for said election as follows: One set of ballots shall have plainly printed or written thereon the following words: “In favor of the annual levy of one-half of one mill for public library, “Yes;” the other set of ballots shall have plainly written or printed thereon the following words: “In favor of the annual levy of one-half of one mill for public library, No.” § 3. Oath for Trustees.—Before holding said election the said Trustees shall subscribe to the oath usually provided for in case of managers of general elections, which oath shall be taken before the Clerk of the Court and filed in his office for record. 

§ 4. Tax Levy—Disbursement.—If a majority of the ballots cast at such election be in favor of said annual levy, said Trustees shall make return thereof to the County Auditor of Lancaster County, under oath, stating the true number of ballots cast in favor and against the same, which return shall become a perma- nent record of his office, and said Auditor and his successors in office be, and are hereby authorized and required, annually thereafter, to levy upon all the property returned for taxation within said school district, one-half of one mill on the dollar, and the County Treasurer collect the same, as a special fund for the maintenance of a public library therein, to be paid to the Trustees, or other authorized officers of such public library, upon their warrant.


Year:1916       ACT NO.:626
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE ELECTION OF SCHOOL DISTRICT TRUSTEES IN LANCASTER AND SALUDA AND KERSHAW COUNTIES.

Section 1. Election for Trustees - Terms - Ballot - Proviso.- Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina : The County Boards of Education of the counties of Lancaster and Saluda and Kershaw are hereby authorized and directed to order in each school district of the county an election for public school trustees to be held on the first Saturday in May , 1916. At said election there shall be chosen from the qualified electors residing in the district three trustees , who shall designate by lot , one member to serve for one year , a sec- ond member to serve for two years , and a third member to serve for three years . Annually thereafter the said County Board of Education shall order an election in each school district , at which one trustee shall be chosen for a term of three years , and until his successor shall have been elected and qualified . At any election herein authorized , the Board of School District Trustees shall act as managers , shall count the ballots , declare the result and report same in writing to the County Board of Education , and any and all elections for said school District Trustees shall be held under the rules regulating general elec- tions for State and County officers . At any election for School District Trustees , every qualified elector residing in said school district shall be entitled to vote : Provided , That the County Board of Education for Kershaw County shall order such elec- tion only in such school districts as lie partly in Kershaw and partly in Lancaster Counties .

§ 2. Oath - Qualification . - Upon notice of election , any trustee shall take and subscribe the oath of office prescribed by Section 26 , Article III of the Constitution of this State . Said oath shall be administered free of charge by the County Superintendent of Education , and shall be kept on file in the County Superintend- ent's office . Any trustee failing to qualify within thirty days after the date of his election shall be disqualified for trusteeship and the vacancy thus created shall be filled as hereinafter pro- vided . All Commissions of trustees shall be issued by the County Board of Education upon the filing of the oath of qualification .

§ 3. Vacancies - Removals . Any and all vacancies from death , resignation , removal or otherwise shall be filled by the County Board of Education for the unexpired term . The County Board is further authorized to suspend or remove from office any District Trustee upon the assignment of written cause after a public hearing , and to fill the vacancy thus created by the appointment of a successor to fill out the unexpired term .

§ 4. Powers - Duties . - All the powers and duties now devolved upon School District Trustees shall continue to be exercised by the Trustees herein authorized to be elected . Nothing in this Act contained shall be construed to effect any existing school district organized and operated under a special Act of the Gen- eral Assembly , and it is expressly declared that this Act shall apply only to public school districts organized and operated under the general school law of the State .

§ 5. Inconsistent Acts Repealed . - All Acts and parts of Acts inconsistent with this Act , be , and the same are hereby , repealed . Approved Feb. 19 , 1916 .

AN ACT TO AMEND AN ACT ENTITLED ""AN ACT TO AMEND THE LAW AS TO THE ELECTION, POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE TRUSTEES OF THE GRADED SCHOOL DISTRICT OF THE TOWN OF BISHOPVILLE,"" APPROVED THE 22D DAY OF FEBRUARY, A. D. 1904, SO AS TO FURTHER REGULATE THE ELECTION AND TERM OF OFFICE OF THE TRUSTEES FOR SAID SCHOOL DISTRICT.

Section 1. Election of Trustees Number Term . - Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina :
That Section 2 of an Act entitled " An Act to amend the law as to the election , powers and duties of the Trustees of the Graded School District of the town of Bishopville , " approved the 22d day of February , 1904 , be amended by striking out the words , " Whose term of office shall be for two years and until their suc- cessors are elected , said election to be held on the second Tuesday in April , 1905 " and by inserting in lieu thereof the following : " Consisting of five members said election to be held on the second Tuesday in April , 1917 , " and by inserting after the words , " Every second year thereafter , " the following : " The trustees elected at the election held under this Act shall determine their term of office by lot , so that one of said trustees shall hold office for two years , two of said trustees for four years and two of said trustees for six years ; and that thereafter the term of office of each trus- tee shall be for a period of six years , " so that said Section 2 of said Act shall read as follows :

Section 2. That the School Trustees of said School District shall have power and they are hereby required to call a meeting of the qualified electors of said school district for the purpose of electing a Board of Trustees for said school district consisting of five members , said election to be held on the second Tuesday in April , 1917 , and on the same day of every second year there- after , the Trustees elected at the election held under this Act shall determine their term of office by lot , so that one of said trustees shall hold his office for two years , two of said trustees for four years , two of said trustees for six years ; and that there- after the term of office of each trustee shall be for a period of six years . The trustees shall appoint the managers and publish a notice of said election for at least two weeks previous thereto in one or more newspapers published in the county , and post the same in one or more conspicuous places in said school district . In addition to the duties and responsibilities now pro- vided by law for the trustees of school districts , the said Trustees shall have the following powers and duties , to wit : To purchase and erect suitable buildings for the use of the public schools of the said School District , to elect and dismiss superintendents and teachers of the schools of the district , prescribe their duties , terms of office , and to fix their salaries , and to cause an examina- tion of said teachers to be made whenever in their judgment it is necessary ; to determine the class of books and studies to be used in said schools , and to make rules and regulations for the gov- ernment of said schools ; to determine the manner in which the tax heretofore authorized and the three mills constitutional and poll tax provided by law shall be expended in maintaining said public schools , and to fill all vacancies occurring in said Board of Trustees by death , resignation , removal , refusal to qualify , or otherwise , during their term of office or service ; to grant high school diplomas to pupils finishing the high school course in the white school , and to make an annual report to the State Super- intendent of Education as to the schools as is required of Trus- tees of the county schools ; and to take in charge and keep in order all buildings and property used for school purposes in said district ; to determine the manner in which the tax provided for shall be expended in maintaining the schools of the district ; to assess and collect from each pupil in the white school an inci- dental fee which shall not exceed two dollars ( $ 2.00 ) per ses- sion : Provided , That no pupil shall be deprived of the privileges of school on account of inability to pay the contingent fee .

§ 2. Immediately Effective . This Act shall go into effect . immediately upon its approval by the Governor .


Year:1916       ACT NO.:632
AN ACT TO ENABLE MARLBORO COUNTY TO ESTABLISH AND MAINTAIN PUBLIC HOSPITALS, LEVY TAXES, AND BORROW MONEY THERE-FOR, ELECT HOSPITAL TRUSTEES AND MAINTAIN TRAINING SCHOOLS FOR NURSES.

Section 1. May Have Hospital.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That the citizens of Marlboro County, in the State , may establish and maintain in said County a public hospital, levy a tax and borrow money therefor, elect trustees and maintain a training school for nurses, in the manner hereinafter provided. § 2. Petition for Election—Election—Money May Be Bor- rowed.—Said county may establish a public hospital in the fol- lowing manner: Whenever the Board of County Commissioners shall be presented with a petition signed by four hundred (400) resident freeholders of the County, two hundred (200) of whom shall be qualified electors, and three hundred (300) of whom shall not be residents of the city, town or village where it is proposed to locate such public hospital, asking that an annual tax may be levied for the establishment and maintenance of a public hospital at a public place in the County named therein, and shall specify in their petition the maximum amount of money proposed to be expended in purchasing or building said hospital, such Board of County Commissioners shall submit the question to the qualified electors of the County at the next general elec- tion to be held in the County, or, at a special election called for that purpose, first giving ninety days’ notice thereof in one or more newspapers published in the County, if any be published therein, and by posting such notice, written or printed, in each township of the County, which notice shall include the text of the petition, and state the amount of the tax to be levied upon the assessed property of the said County, which tax shall not exceed two mills on the dollar for the purchase of a site or sites, and the erection thereon of a public hospital building; and for the sup- port of same; which said election shall be held at the usual places in such County for electing County officers, the vote to be canvassed in the same maner as for other County officers: Pro- vided, The County Commissioners are authorized and empow- ered by this Act to borrow money for the purpose of purchasing a site and establishing and maintaining said hospital, and pledge 

the taxes which shall be levied under this Act as security for such money borrowed: Provided, further, That no sum of money shall be borrowed in excess of the amount which shall be received from taxes levied for hospital purposes during the current year in which such money is borrowed. § 3. Conduct of Election —The Board of County Commission- ers of said County shall submit to the qualified electors thereof, at a regular or special election, the question whether there shall be levied upon the assessed property of such County a tax of two mills on the dollar for the purchase of real estate for hospital purposes, for the construction of hospital buildings, and for maintaining same, or for either or all of such purposes. The ballots to be used at such election at which the hospital question is submitted shall be printed with a statement substantially as follows: For a two-mill tax on the dollar for a public hospital and for maintenance of same—‘ YES.” For a two-mill tax on the dollar for a public hos- pital and for maintenance of same—“NO.” If a majority of votes cast at such election on the proposition so submitted shall be in favor of a two-mill tax for a public hospital and for maintenance of same, the Board of County Commissioners shall levy the tax so authorized which shall be collected in the same manner as other taxes are collected, and credited to the “Hospital Fund,” and shall be paid out on the order of the hospital trustees for the purpose authorized by this Act, and for no other purposes whatever. § 4. Appointment of Trustees—Terms—Proviso.—Should a majority of all the votes cast upon the question be in favor of estab- lishing such County hospital, then the Governor, by and with the consent of a majority of the delegation from the County in which such hospital is to be located, shall appoint seven (7) trustees chosen with reference to their fitness for such office, three (3) of whom may be women, but all of said trustees must be residents of the County; not more than four (4) of said trustees to be residents of The the city, town or village in which said hospital is to be located. trustees appointed as provided in this section shall constitute a board of trustees of said public hospital. The said trustees shall hold their offices for the following terms: Two (2) for two years, two (2) for four years, and three (3) for six years, and until their successors are appointed and qualified; the respective terms of the trustees originally appointed shall be determined by lot. Any vacancy that may occur in the Board of Trustees shall be filled by appointment in the same manner as the original trustees are 

appointed, and any such appointee shall hold office for the unex- pired term only: Provided, No practicing physician can hold the office of trustee of any hospital created under the terms of this Act. § 5. Duties of Trustees—Rules—Subordinates—Meetings— Report—Proviso.—The said trustees shall, within ten days after their appointment or election, qualify by taking the oath of civil officers and organize as a Board of Hospital Trustees by the elec- tion of one of their number as a chairman, one as secretary and by the election of such other officers as they may deem necessary, but no bond shall be required of them. The County Treasurer of the County in which said hospital is located shall be Treasurer of the Board of Trustees. The Treasurer shall receive and pay out all moneys under the control of said board, as directed by it, but shall receive no compensation from such board. No trustee shall receive any compensation for his services performed, but he may receive reimbursement for any cash expenditure actually made for per- sonal expenses incurred as such trustee, and an itemized statement of all such expenses and money paid out shall be made under oath by each of such trustees and filed with the secretary, and allowed only by the affirmative vote of all the trustees present at a meeting of the board. The Board of Hospital Trustees shall make and adopt such by-laws, rules and regulations for their own guidance and for the government of the hospital as may be deemed expedient for the economic and equitable conduct thereof, not inconsistent with this Act and the ordinances of the city or town wherein such public hospital is located. They shall have the exclusive control of the expenditure of all moneys collected to the credit of the hos- pital fund, and the purchase of site or sites, the purchase or con- struction of any hospital building or buildings, and the supervision, care and custody of the grounds, rooms or buildings purchased, con- structed, leased or set apart for the purpose: Provided, That all moneys received for such hospital shall be deposited in the treasury of the County to the credit of the hospital fund, and paid out only upon warrants drawn by the Auditor of said County upon properly authenticated vouchers of the hospital board. Said Board of Hos- pita! Trustees shall have power to appoint a suitable superintendent or matron, or both, and necessary assistants, and fix their compen- sation, and shall also have the power to remove such appointees: and shall in general carry out the spirit and intent of this Act in establishing and maintaining a County public hospital, with equal 

rights to all and special privileges to none. Such Board of Hospital Trustees shall hold meetings at least once each month, shall keep a complete record of all its proceedings; and four (4) members of such board shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of busi- ness. One of said trustees shall visit and examine said hospital at least twice each month, and the board shall, during the first week of January in each year, file with the Board of County Commis- sioners of said County a report of their proceedings with reference to such hospital, and a statement of all receipts and expenditures during the year; and shall at such time certify the amount necessary to maintain and improve such hospital for the ensuing year. No trustee shall have a personal pecuniary interest, either directly or indirectly, in the purchase of any supplies for said hospital, unless the same are purchased by competitive bidding. § 6. Vacancies.—Vacancies in the Board of Trustees occa- sioned by removals, resignations or otherwise, shall be reported to the Board of County Commissioners and be filled in like manner as original appointments, appointees to hold office until the next following general election, when such vacancies shall be filled by election in the usual manner. § 7. Condemnation Authorized.—If the Board of Hospital Trustees and the owners of any property desired by them for hos- pital purposes cannot agree as to the price to be paid therefor, they shall report the fact to the Board of County Commissioners and condemnation proceedings shall be instituted by the Board of County Commissioners and prosecuted in the name of the County wherein such public hospital is to be located, by the County attor- ney for such County, in the same manner as land is now condemned by the County Commissioners for the opening, changing or estab- lishing public roads in the State  § 8. Prerequisites to Erection.—No hospital building shall be erected or constructed until the plans and specifications have been made therefor and adopted by the Board of Hospital Trustees, and bids advertised for according to law for other county buildings. § 9. Under Municipal Jurisdiction—The jurisdiction of the city, town or village in or near which public hospital is located shall extend over all lands used for hospital purposes outside the cor- porate limits, if so located, and all ordinances of such cities and towns shall be in full force and effect in and over the territory occu- pied by such public hospital. 

§ 10. County May Appropriate Aid—The Board of County Commissioners may appropriate each year, in addition to tax for hospital fund hereinbefore provided for, not exceeding five (5) per cent. of its general fund for the improvements and maintenance of any public hospital so established. § 11. Who to Receive Benefits —The hospital established under this Act shall be for the benefit of the inhabitants of Marl- boro County and of any person falling sick or being injured or maimed within its limits; but every inhabitant or person who is not a pauper shall pay to such Board of Hospital Trustees, or such officers as it shall designate for such County public hospital, a rea- sonable compensation for occupancy, nursing, care, medicine or attendance, according to the rules and regulations prescribed by said board, such hospital always being subject to such reasonable rules and regulations as said board may adopt, in order to render the use of said hospital of the greatest benefit to the greatest num- ber; and said board may exclude from the use of such hospital any and all inhabitants and persons who shall wilfully violate such rules and regulations. And said board may extend the privileges and use of such hospital to persons residing outside of such County. upon such terms and conditions as said board may from time to time, by its rules and regulations prescribe: Provided, Such hospital shall be so arranged as to separate the white race from the colored Trace, § 12. Rules of Hospital to Govern.—When such hospital is established, the physicians, nurses, attendants, the persons sick therein, and all persons approaching or coming within the limits of same, and all furniture and other articles used or brought there. shall be subject to such rules and regulations as said board may pre- scribe. § 13. Donations Permissible——Any person or persons, firm, organization, corporation or society desiring to make donations of money, personal property or real estate for the benefit of such hos- pital, shall have the right to vest title of the money or real estate so donated in said County to be controlled, when accepted, by the Board of Hospital Trustees, according to the terms of the deed, gift, devise, or bequest of such property. § 14. No Discrimination as to Physicians—Attending Physi- cian in Control.—In the management of such public hospital no discrimination shall be made against practitioners of any school of medicine recognized by the laws , and all such 

legal practitioners shall have equal privileges in treating patients in such hospital. The patients shall have the absolute right to employ at his or her own expense, his or her physician, and when acting for any patient in such hospital the physician employed by such patient shall have exclusive charge of the care and treatment of such patient, and nurses therein shall as to such patient be subject to the directions of such physician, subject always to such rules and regu- lations as shall be established by the Board of Trustees under the provision of this Act. § 15. May Have Nurses’ Training School—The Board of Trus- tees of said County public hospital may establish and maintain a connection therewith and as a part of said public hospital, a train- ing school for nurses. § 16. Provision for Insane—The said Board of Trustees shall at all times provide a suitable room for the detention and examina- tion of all persons who are brought before the Commissioners of Insanity for such County: Provided, That such hospital is located at the County seat. § 17. Accommodations for Tubercular Patients—The Board of Trustees of said hospital are hereby authorized to provide a department of said public hospital, but not necessarily attached thereto, suitable accommodation and means for the care and treat- ment of persons suffering from tuberculosis, and to formulate such rules and regulations for the government of such persons, and for the protection from infection of other patients and the nurses and attendants in such public hospital as they may deem necessary ; and it shall be the duty of all persons in charge of or employed at such hospitals, or residents thereof, to faithfully obey and comply with any and all such rules and regulations. Said Board of Hospital Trustees shall, if practicable, employ as head nurse to be placed in charge of said public tuberculosis sanatorium, one who has had experience in the management and care of tuberculosis persons. § 18. Charity Patients—The Board of Hospital Trustees shall have the power to determine whether or not patients presented at said public hospital for treatment are objects of charity, and shall fix the price for compensation for such patients, and shall pay the same out of the County hospital fund. § 19. May Contract for Care of Tuberculosis Patients.—The Board of County Commissioners of said County, where no suitable provision has been made for the care of indigent tuberculosis resi- dents, may contract with the Board of Hospital Trustees of any 

public hospital for the care of such persons in the sanatorium department of such hospital, upon such reasonable terms as may be agreed upon. § 20. Immediately Effective —That this Act shall go into effect immediately upon the approval of the Governor. 


Year:1916       ACT NO.:639
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 14 IN NEWBERRY COUNTY TO ISSUE BONDS TO ENLARGE AND FURTHER EQUIP THE SCHOOLHOUSE THEREIN.

Section 1. Bond Issue—Election.—Be it enacted by the Gen- eral Assembly of the State : That the School Trustees of School District No. 14 in Newberry County, embrac- ing the town of Prosperity are hereby authorized and required to issue coupon bonds to the amount of Thirty-Five Hundred Dollars, payable in eight years, for the purpose of enlarging and further equipping the School House in said School District, pro- vided that a majority of the qualified electors of said School 

OU District shall vote in favor of such issue at an election to be held hereafter at such time as muy be fixed by the said Trustees. § 2. Conduct of Election.—That the Trustees of said School District are hereby required to order an election on the question of the issue of said bonds and to give three weeks previous notice in one or more of the newspapers published in the county of Newberry, or in three or more public places in said School District of the time of such election, and they are further authorized to appoint managers and to prescribe the form of ballots and to receive the returns and to declare the result of such election. § 3. Denomination of Bonds—Signature—Non-Taxable.—That said School District is hereby declared a body corporate, for the purpose of executing and issuing said bonds and other powers herein given in case their issue be authorized by said election. The said bonds shall be issued in such denominations as the Trus- tees of said School District shall deem best, and shall be paya- ble five years from the date of their issue, with interest payable annually, at a rate not to exceed six per cent. per annum. The said bonds and coupons shall be signed. by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of said School District and countersigned by its secretary, and their coupons shall be receivable in payment of any taxes in said school district. The said bonds shall be exempt from taxation for State, County or municipal purposes. § 4. Tax Levy—Sinking Fund.—That for the purpose of pay- ing the interest accruing on said bonds, and for the purpose of creating a sinking fund for the payment of the principal of said bonds, the County Auditor of Newberry County, or such other officer who may be charged with the assessment of taxes, shall annually levy a tax of two mills on all taxable real or personal property in said school district, and the amount so levied shall be collected by the County Treasurer of Newberry County as State and county taxes are collected, to be held and applied by him for the purpose aforesaid, and shall be used for no other pur- pose whatsoever. The surplus remaining after the payment of the annual interest on said bonds shall be a sinking fund for the payment of the principal of said bonds and shall be kept on deposit, at interest, by County Treasurer in the banks of the said school district. § 5. Deposit of Proceeds—How to Be Used.—That the said Board of Trustees are authorized and empowered to sell said bonds at their par value, and shall deposit all money coming to 

them from such sale in bank to the credit of said Board, and they shall use the said money exclusively for the purpose set out in Section 1 of this Act, and should any of said bonds be not used they shall be cancelled by the said Board of Trustees. § 6. Disposition of Surplus.—That any surplus remaining after the payment of said bonds be transferred from the Sinking Fund to the current funds of the school district, to be used for the maintenance of the schools therein. § 7. Immediately Effective —This Act shall take effect imme- diately upon its approval by the Governor. 


Year:1916       ACT NO.:648
AN ACT RELATING TO SCHOOL TRUSTEES IN SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 3, OF ORANGEBURG COUNTY.

Section 1. Election of Trustees.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That there shall be elected by the qualified electors residing in School District No. 3, known as the Four Holes School District, in the County of Orangeburg, three trustees who shall go into office at the expira- tion of the term of office of the present trustees. The three trus- tees so elected shall determine among themselves by lot their respective terms of office so that one trustee shall serve for one year, one for two years and one for three years and one trustee shall go out of office each year thereafter, and their successors shall be annually elected for a term of three years each. The County Board of Education shall annually order said election and give notice of such election for two weeks and shall appoint wt managers to manage such elections. The managers of said elec- tion shall conduct the same as general elections are conducted, and shall make returns thereof to the County Board of Education of Orangeburg County, who shall declare the result thereof; and it shall be the duty of the said County Board of Education to issue a certificate of election to the trustee or trustees so elected. 
 

Year:1916       ACT NO.:649
AN ACT TO ENABLE THE COUNTY OF ORANGEBURG TO ESTABLISH AND MAINTAIN A PUBLIC HOSPITAL, AND TO PROVIDE FOR A TAX TO SUPPORT THE SAME, UPON AN ELECTION IN SUCH
COUNTY IN FAVOR THEREOF.

Section 1. Public Hospital May Be Established.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That a public hospital may be established and maintained in the County of Orangeburg upon a vote in favor thereof by a majority of the qualified electors of said County, at an election ordered and held as hereinafter provided, and a tax shall then be levied therefor upon conditions hereinafter provided. § 2. Conduct of Election—Tax Levy.—Upon petition filed with the County Board of Commissioners for the County of Orange- burg, signed by not less than four hundred registered electors of said county asking that an election be ordered upon the question of establishing and maintaining a public hospital for the County of Orangeburg, and asking that an annual tax may be levied for the establishment and maintenance of such hospital, not exceed- ing two mills on the dollar of the property in said county, and stating the amount of such proposed levy, it shall be the duty of the County Board of Commissioners to order an election in said County and give notice of sixty days thereof in one or more newspapers in said County and such election shall be conducted by the proper officers now provided by law for conducting general elections, who shall appoint managers to conduct the same, and they shall canvass and declare the result, and the said managers shall conduct the said election as general elections are conducted in this State, and all qualified electors residing in said County shall be allowed to vote. Upon a majority of the qualified elec- tors in said County voting in favor of the establishment and main- tenance of such hospital in said County, and in favor of the tax levy for such purposes, it shall be the duty of the proper officers of said County to levy said tax in such amount as may be author- ized in such election annually for a term of two years; and there- after annually for three years to levy a tax of one-half of the annual levy ordered for the first two years; and then the County Board of Commissioners shall order an annual levy of not exceed- ing one-half mill, as they may deem necessary, for the mainte- 

nance and support of the said hospital, to be collected as other taxes are collected in said county. § 3. Trustees.—That in the event the election shall be in favor of the establishment and maintenance of such hospital there shall be a board of seven trustees, appointed by the Governor, upon the recommendation of the members of the General Assembly from such County, three of whom shall be appointed for six years, two for four years and two for two years, and until their succes- sors are elected and qualified, and whose successors shall be appointed in like manner for a term of six years each. Any vacancy that may occur in the Board of Trustees shall be filled by appointment in like manner for the unexpired term only. § 4. Powers of Trustees.—As soon as may be practicable after their appointment the said Trustees shall meet and organize, as a Board of Hospital Trustees for the County of Orangeburg, by electing one of their number as Chairman and one as Secretary, and they may elect a Treasurer and require of him such bond as they may deem necessary. No Trustee shall receive any compen- sation for his services as a member of the Board, other than his actual necessary expenses incurred in attending the meetings of the Board, and the expenses incurred under direction of the Board in otherwise performing the duties of his office. No mem- ber of said Board of Hospital Trustees shall be an employee of the said Board, or hold a salaried position in the service of said hospital. The Board of Trustees shall have the power to locate the said hospital at some suitable point in said county, and may purchase property for the purpose of establishing and maintaining such hospital in said County, and may erect such building or buildings thereon as .may be necessary, and make such rules and regula- tions governing and controlling the operation of such hospital as they may deem best, and may ‘change the same from time to time; the said Board shall have the power to employ such super- intendent or matron, or both, and such necessary assistants and employees as may be necessary for the maintenance and support of such hospital, and fix their compensations, and shall have the power to remove such employees at their pleasure ; and shall have power to make such further rules and regulations as they may deem best in carrying out the spirit and intent of this Act in estab- lishing and maintaining an Orangeburg County Public Hospital; and the said Board of Trustees shall hold such meetings for the transaction of business at such regular intervals as may be neces- 

sary and provided in their rules and regulations. All purchases of supplies and property for the construction and use of said hospital shall be by competitive bidding. § 5. Application of Funds.—All taxes levied under this Act for the establishment, maintenance and support of the said hospital shall be collected by the County Treasurer, and the funds so col- lected held by him as a separate fund to be paid out on order of the Board of Hospital Trustees. All claims against the hospital for purchase of property, construction or maintenance shall be itemized and verified, and approved in writing by a majority of the said Board, and all warrants drawn on the County Treasurer against such fund shall be signed by the Chairman of such Board and attested by its Secretary. § 6. Advisory Trustees.—The said Board of Hospital Trustees shall have the power to appoint an advisory Board of Trustees, of such number as in their opinion may be necessary, in order to give representation thereon to such societies, orders, organiza- tions, associations or municipalities as may undertake to con- tribute benefits towards the support and maintenance of the said hospital subject to such rules and regulations as the said Board of Hospital Trustees may adopt; and they may appoint any ladies of the said county to membership on the said advisory Board of Trustees. § 7. Government of Hospital.—The Hospital established under this Act shall be for the benefit of the citizens of the County of Orangeburg, and the said Board of Hospital Trustees may adopt such rules and regulations governing their admission as may be deemed just and reasonable, and they may provide such reason- able fees or compensation to be charged for occupancy, nursing, care, medicine, or attendance, and said hospital shall be operated and governed according to such reasonable rules and regulations, as the said Board may adopt in order to render its uses and bene- fits of the greatest good to the greatest number, and the said Board may exclude from the use of such hospital any and all persons who shall wilfully ‘violate such rules and regulations. And the said Board of Hospital Trustees may extend the privi- leges and uses of the hospital to persons residing outside the County of Orangeburg upon such terms and conditions, and sub- ject to such charges as said Board may from time to time, by its rules and regulations, prescribe preference always being given to 

citizens of Orangeburg County. Such hospital shall be so arranged as to separate the white race from the colored race. § 8. Physicians.—In the management and operation of such hospital no discrimination shall be made against the practitioner of any school of medicine recognized by the laws of South Caro- lina. And all such legal practitioners shall -have equal privileges in treating patients in such hospital. All patients shall have the right to employ at their own expense his or her physician, and in attending any such patient in such hospital the physician, so employed by such patient, shall have the exclusive care and treatment of such patient, subject only to such rules and regula- tions as the Board of Hospital Trustees may prescribe. § 9. Training School for Nurses.—The Board of Hospital Trus- tees may establish and maintain in connection therewith, and as a part of said public hospital, a training school for nurses. § 10. May Accept Gifts.—The said Board of Hospital Trustees is hereby authorized and empowered to accept any contributions or donations of money, personal property or real estate for the benefit of such hospital that may be proffered or made by any person or persons, firm, order society, corporation or association ; and the said Board may accept the same under such terms and conditions as may seem to it desirable. § 11. Trustees to Seek Aid.—The said Board of Hospital Trus- tees shall endeavor to elicit the assistance in the support and maintenance of the hospital of such persons, organizations orders, societies, associations or municipalities as may be deemed a. advisable; and they shall encourage the formation of hospital associations in the various towns or townships of said county in order to obtain such help and assistance as such associations or any individuals may be induced to render in the support and maintenance of such hospital. § 12. Charity Patients —The Board of Hospital Trustees shall admit free of charge such charity patients, as they may be able to provide for, and subject to such rules and regulations as they may adopt ; and they shall fix such charges as they may find necessary to be required of other patients, who are admitted to the benefits of such hospital. And the hospital benefits shall be open to all of the citizens of the county of Orangeburg, who comply with such rules and regulations, and subject to the provisions of this Act. 

§ 13. Expenditures by Trustees.—The said Board of Hospital Trustees are authorized and empowered to borrow money for the purpose of purchasing a site and erecting buildings thereon for establishing and maintaining such hospital and may pledge the tax levy to be made and collected under this Act for the first two years as Security therefor; and they may thereafter borrow from time to time for the further support and maintenance of such hospital and pledge the subsequent taxes to be collected under this Act for hospital purposes, only during the current year in which such money is borrowed and tax levied and collected. And the said Board shall have no further authority to incur any indebtedness or expenses that shall be an obligation of the County ; and they shall have no power to incur any obligation that shall be a lien upon the hospital site, buildings or property. The purpose of this section is to limit the right of the said Board to expend only the amount realized for the said hospital upon the taxes levied therefor under this Act, and the income derived from the patients for uses and benefits of such hospital together with any donation, gifts and cotributions received by them for said hospital. § 14. Immediately Effective—This Act shall go into effect immediately upon its approval by the Governor. 


Year:1916       ACT NO.:651
AN ACT TO AMEND AN ACT ENTITLED “AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A NEW SCHOOL DISTRICT IN THE COUNTY OF ORANGEBURG, AND TO AUTHORIZE THE LEVY AND COLLECTION
OF A SPECIAL SCHOOL TAX THEREIN"" AND ACTS AMENDATORY THEREOF".

Section 1. School May Levy Tax - Election - Trustees - Num- ber - Election - Powers - Vacancies . - Be it enacted by the Gen- eral Assembly of the State of South Carolina : That an Act entitled " An Act to Provide for the Establishment of a new School District in the County of Orangeburg , and to authorize the levy and collection of a special School Tax therein " and Acts amendatory thereof , said School District including the city of Orangeburg , be , and the same are hereby amended by striking out all of Section 3 and Section 4 of said original Act , as amended by an Act approved February 21st , 1903 , and inserting in lieu thereof Section 3 and Section 4 , to read as follows : Section 3 . That in addition to the rights and privileges hereinbefore granted , the said School District shall have the power to levy and collect a special tax on the assessed value of all real and personal prop- erty returned in said School District , not exceeding ten mills on the dollar , subject to the following provisions : Upon the written request of fifty property holders asking that the levy be increased or raised , and stating the amount of the new levy proposed , the trustees of said School District shall , within thirty days from the filing of such request or petition , order an election of the qualified electors in said School District on such question , and give notice thereof for two weeks in one or more newspapers in the city of Orangeburg , and shall appoint the managers of such election , who shall conduct said election as general elections are now held in this State and shall certify the returns thereof to the trustees of said School District . If a majority of those voting in said . election shall vote in favor of the proposed new levy it shall be adopted as the levy for the School District , and continue until changed in the manner herein provided .

Section 4. That the Board of Trustees of said School District shall be composed of five members , and the trustees now in office shall continue until the expiration of their present terms . During the Month of June , 1919 , the Board of Trustees shall order an election in said school district by giving two weeks ' public notice thereof in one or more newspapers published in the city of Orangeburg , and shall appoint managers to conduct such elec- tions , as general elections are held in this State , and there shall be elected five trustees for said School District , three of whom shall serve for a term of two years and two of whom shall serve for a term of four years , the trustees so elected shall determine among themselves by lot within thirty days after the election as to their respective terms of office ; during the month of June in each second year thereafter the said trustees shall order an elec- tion as herein directed for the election of successors to those trus- tees whose terms shall be expiring . All persons residing in such school district and having the qualifications to vote in general elections may vote in such elections . The managers of the elec- tion for trustees , as herein provided , shall certify the result of all such elections to the County Board of Education , who shall meet and declare the result within fifteen days thereafter . The said trustees in addition to the powers and authority now con- ferred on School Trustees , shall have the following powers and . duties : 1. To elect a chairman and Secretary of their Board . 2. To purchase or lease school property and erect school buildings for the use of the public schools of said school district . 3. To elect and dismiss superintendents and teachers of the said school ; to prescribe their duties , terms of office , and to fix their salaries , and to cause an examination of said teachers to be made when- ever necessary ; also to determine the class books and course of studies to be used in said school , and to make rules and regula- tions for the government of said school . 4. To determine the manner in which the tax heretofore authorized and the other school funds of said district shall be expended in maintaining said public school .

5. To fill all vacancies occurring in said Board of Trustees by death , resignation , removal or otherwise , until the next elec- tion for Trustees shall be held , when any such vacancy shall then be filled by election either for the balance of the unexpired term or for the full term as the case may be .

§ 2. Inconsistent Acts Repealed . - All Acts or parts of Acts inconsistent herewith are hereby repealed .


Year:1916       ACT NO.:652
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE AND EMPOWER ELLOREE HIGH AND GRADED SCHOOL DISTRICT IN THE COUNTY OF ORANGEBURG, TO CHARGE A MATRICULATION FEE.

Section 1. School May Charge Matriculation Fee - Certain Pupils Excepted . - Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of South Carolina : That the Board of Trustees of the Elloree High and Graded School , being designated as School District No. 70 , in Orangeburg County , are hereby authorized and empowered to charge and collect an incidental or matricula- tion fee from each pupil , not exceeding two dollars per annum the same to be payable at such times and in such installments as the said trustees may require . The said fees may be used for the purposes of heating , repairing and lighting the school build- ing , for janitors ' service , for fire insurance , and other incidental expenses : Provided , That no pupil shall be prohibited from attending the school for failure to pay the said incidental or matriculation fee , upon satisfactory showing to the said trustees of the inability of such pupil or his or her parent or guardian to pay the same .


Year:1916       ACT NO.:655
AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR ORDERING AN ELECTION ON THE QUESTION OF TRANSFERRING SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 2, IN ORANGEBURG COUNTY, TO SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 70, AND TO AUTHORIZE THE
TRANSFER UPON COMPLIANCE WITH CERTAIN CONDITIONS.

Section 1. Election for Transfer of School District—Conduct of Election.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That upon petition being filed with the County Board of Education for the County of Orangeburg by twenty quali- fied electors residing in school District No. 2, of the County of Orangeburg, it shall be the duty of the said County Board of Edu- cation to order an election in said school district upon the question of the transfer and annexation of school district No. 2 with Special School District No. 70, known as the Elloree School District, and the said County Board of Education shall designate the time and place of holding such election, shall appoint managers to conduct the same, and shall give two weeks public notice thereof; the said managers shall conduct the said election as general elections are con- ducted in this State, and all qualified electors residing in said school district No. 2 shall be entitled to vote; and the said managers shall forthwith make returns of such election to the County Board of Education. § 2. Annexation of District——That in the event a majority of the qualified electors, voting in said election shall vote in favor of the transfer and annexation of School District No. 2, of the County of Orangeburg, to said School District No. 70, known as the Elloree School District, it shall be the duty of the County Board of Educa- tion, for the County of Orangeburg, to pass an order directing that said school district No. 2, be transferred and annexed to the said school district No. 70 in which event the said school district No. 2 shall then compose a part of school district No. 70, with all the 

rights, powers, privileges and liabilities now or hereafter imposed by law upon said school district No. 70 known as the Elloree School District. § 3. Immediately Effective—This Act shall go into effect immediately upon its approval by the Governor. 


Year:1916       ACT NO.:660
AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE SCHOOL COMMISSIONERS FOR THE SCHOOL DISTRICT OF THE CITY OF COLUMBIA TO ORDER, AND HOLD AN ELECTION FOR LEVYING A SPECIAL TAX FOR SCHOOL PURPOSES.

Section 1. Election for School Tax Levy.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That the School Commissioners for the School District of the City of Columbia, County of Richland, and State , be, and they are hereby, authorized and empowered to submit to the qualified electors of said School District not later than March Sixteenth, A. D., 1916, the question of levying an annual tax of five mills on the taxable property in said School District, to be used for the current expenses incurred for the support and main- tenance of the schools in said District. 

§ 2. Conduct of Election.—That the said School Commission- ers of the School District of the City of Columbia shall order an election upon the said question to be held at such place, or places. in the School District as may be designated by the said School Commissioners, and shall give notice of such election for ten days in a newspaper published in said District, which notice shall designate the time and place, or places, at which the election will be held, and the said School Commissioners shall appoint the managers of said election, receive the returns, and declare the result. § 3. Form of Ballot—That the School Commissioners shall have printed and provided for the use of the voters a sufficient number of ballots, which shall be placed at the voting place, or places, on which shall be printed the question to be submitted and the words “Yes” and “No,” so that the voter may indicate his vote by striking out one or the other of the words on said ballot, and the word not so stricken out to be counted. § 4. Assessment of Tax.—That if a majority of the votes cast at such an election shall be in favor of levying the said tax, the School Commissioners shall certify the fact to the County Auditor who shall thereupon annually assess said tax on the taxable property of said School District and enter the same upon the tax duplicates, and the County Treasurer shall thereupon collect said taxes at the same time and in the same manner as other taxes. § 5. Disbursement of Proceeds.—That the County Treasurer shall keep a separate account of said taxes and shall pay all moneys realized and collected on account of same to the School Commissioners for the School District of the City of Columbia, to be used for the purposes aforesaid. § 6. School Commissioners May Borrow Money.—That the School Commissioners of said School District are authorized to borrow money on account of said taxes, if same shall be voted for the purposes aforesaid, and to pledge said taxes for the pay- ment of such money as they may borrow. § 7. Immediately Effective—That this act shall go into effect immediately upon its approval by the Governor. 


Year:1916       ACT NO.:666
AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE SCHOOL TRUSTEES OF EACH AND EVERY SCHOOL DISTRICT IN THE COUNTY OF RICHLAND TO ORDER AND HOLD AN ELECTION FOR LEVYING A SPECIAL TAX FOR SCHOOL PURPOSES.

Section 1. Election for Special School Tax Authorized.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : That the School Trustees of each and every School District in the County of Richland, and State  be, and they are hereby, authorized and empowered to submit to the qualified elec- tors of their respective School Districts, not later than June Ist, A. D. 1916, the question of levying an annual tax on all the taxable property in said School District to be used for the current expenses incurred for the support and maintenance of the School in said dis- trict. § 2. Conduct of Election.—That the said School Trustees for each and every district shall order an election upon the said ques- tion to be held at such place, or places, in the School District as may be designated by the said School Trustees, and shall give notice of such election for ten days in some newspaper published in the County of Richland, and by posting a notice of such election at three prominent places in the School District, to be selected by the School Trustees, which notice shall designate the time and place or places, at which the election will be held, and the said School Trustees shall appoint the managers of said election, receive the returns, and declare the result. 

§ 3. Form of Ballot—That the School Trustees shall have printed and provided for the use of the voters a sufficient number of ballots which shall be placed at the voting place, or places, on which shall be printed the question to be submitted and which shall state definitely the amount of the tax levy to be voted upon, which amount shall be determined by the said School Trustees, and the words “Yes” and “No,” so that the voter may indicate his vote by striking out one or the other of the words on said ballot, and the word not so stricken out to be counted. § 4. Tax Levy.—That if a majority of the votes cast at such an election shall be in favor of levying the said tax, the School Trus- tees shall certify the fact to the County Auditor who shall thereupon annually assess said tax on the taxable property of said School Dis- trict and enter the same upon the tax duplicates, and the County ‘Treasurer shall thereupon collect said taxes at the same time and in the same manner as other taxes. § 5. Trustees to Receive Proceeds.—That the County Treasurer shall keep a separate account of said taxes and shall pay all moneys realized and collected on account of same to the School Trustees for the School District for which said tax has been levied, to be used for the purposes aforesaid. § 6. Trustees May Borrow Money.—That the School Trustees of any School District are authorized to borrow money on account of said taxes, if same shall be voted for the purposes aforesaid, and to pledge said taxes for the payment of such money as they may borrow. § 7. Immediately Effective—That this Act shall go into effect immediately upon its approval by the Governor.

Year:1916       ACT NO.:687
AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF TAXES IN FORT MILL SCHOOL DISTRICT, IN YORK COUNTY, FOR A SINKING FUND TO RETIRE BONDS AND MAINTAIN SCHOOLS OF SAID DISTRICT.

Section 1. Annual Levy for Sinking Fund—Increase.—Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State : After the approval of this Act, the County Auditor of York County shall levy and the County Treasurer shall collect annually one mill on the dollar of the assessed value of all property within Fort Mill School District of York County for the purpose of pay- ing the interest and retiring at maturity the Bonds of said District heretofore issued in aid of schools therein and six mills annually for the maintenance of the schools of said District: Provided, That if at the expiration of ten years, it becomes apparent that the amount accumulating, as such Sinking Fund, will not be sufficient to retire said Bonds at maturity, the said levy shall be increased to such amount as will prove sufficient therefor, and the levy for the maintenance of said schools shall be proportionately decreased.
